definition_zh: 不动；静止；无法移动；（社会）停滞；固定不变
definition_en: the state of not being able to move, or the condition of staying fixed in one place
core_image: 石化的脚：明明想迈步，脚却牢牢粘在地上
scene: 车祸之后，伤者的双腿被夹在变形的座椅里，只能等待救援。After the crash, the driver was trapped in complete immobility until rescuers arrived.
sceneCN: 这里 immobility 是「无法移动」（第 1 个义项：身体或物体动不了）；句意：车祸后，司机完全无法动弹，直到救援人员赶到。

pos.zh: 停滞；固定不变（抽象状态）

collocations.zh: 社会流动性不足；阶层固化

derivatives.zh: in- 否定前缀加 mobile 构成，意为「不能移动的；一动不动的」
immobile 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使固定；使无法行动」
immobilize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，指「固定处理；使失去行动能力」
去否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「流动性；移动能力」，与 immobility 构成反义

senses.title: The inability of the body to move
senses.definition: the state in which a person or animal cannot move some or all of the body, because of injury, illness or restraint
senses.definitionCN: 由于受伤、疾病或束缚，人或动物的全部或部分身体无法活动的状态
senses.example: Weeks of immobility after the operation weakened the muscles in his legs.
senses.exampleCN: 手术后数周无法活动，使他腿部肌肉变得无力。
senses.why: In- denies, mobilis means movable, and -ity names a state, so the word literally names the condition of being unable to move.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表否定，mobilis 意为「可动的」，-ity 标识状态，因此这个词字面就是「不能活动的状态」，画面是一个连脚都迈不出去的人。

senses.title: Stillness of things
senses.definition: the condition of an object or machine staying perfectly still, especially when it should be moving
senses.definitionCN: 物体或机器完全静止不动的状况，尤指本应运转时停下不动
senses.example: The frozen crowd could not break the immobility of the traffic.
senses.exampleCN: 凝固的车流让交通完全停摆。
senses.why: Once in- and -ity are attached to a movable thing, the same state can be said of traffic, water or machines that have stopped dead.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「不能动」的状态，也可以说给车流、水或机器，于是从人的身体扩展到一切本该运动却停住的东西。

senses.title: Social stagnation
senses.definition: the condition of little change in a society or an economy, with people unable to rise to a better position
senses.definitionCN: 社会或经济几乎不变、人们难以提升到更好地位的状态
senses.example: Social immobility keeps working-class children from advancing.
senses.exampleCN: 社会阶层固化使工人家庭的孩子难以向上发展。
senses.why: The concrete picture of legs that cannot move becomes the image of people who cannot climb the social ladder.
senses.whyCN: 腿迈不动这一具体画面，被投射到社会层面：人无法沿社会阶梯向上爬，于是有了「阶层固化」的抽象义。

senses.title: A fixed or unalterable state
senses.definition: the quality of staying fixed and unchanging, especially of rules, prices or assets that cannot be shifted
senses.definitionCN: 保持固定、不被改变的性质，尤指规则、价格或资产无法调动
senses.example: The immobility of capital blocked investment in the smaller towns.
senses.exampleCN: 资本缺乏流动性，阻碍了对小城镇的投资。
senses.why: If nothing can be moved, nothing can be changed either, so the word also names anything locked into place.
senses.whyCN: 东西既然动不了，也就改不了；这一引申把物理上的「移动不了」推成抽象上的「变动不了」，资本、规则、价格都适用。

intro.en: Immobility is the negative noun of mobile, built in English from the Latin stem mob-, mov-, meaning to move, with the negating prefix in- and the state suffix -ity.
intro.cn: immobility 是 mobile 的否定名词，由英语在拉丁词干 mob-、mov- 之上构成；词干意为「移动」，前缀 in- 表否定，后缀 -ity 表状态。

items.en: Movere means to move, and its adjective mobilis describes what can be moved; immobilitas names the opposite state.
items.cn: 拉丁语 movere 意为移动，形容词 mobilis 指「能被移动的」，其反面状态即 immobilitas。

items.en: Immobilitas is recorded in late Latin as a noun for want of movement or change.
items.cn: immobilitas 见于晚期拉丁语，作名词表示「不移动、不变化」。

items.en: French mobile and the noun mobilite carry the movable stem forward, with immobilite alongside.
items.cn: 法语 mobile 与 mobilite 把「可动」的词干传下去，immobilite 与之并行。

items.en: English adopts mobility and immobility from French forms of the Latin stem.
items.cn: 英语从法语形态借入 mobility 与 immobility，二者都回到拉丁词干。

items.en: Immobile follows as the adjective, and the pair settles into medical and mechanical use.
items.cn: immobile 随后作为形容词出现，这一对词逐渐进入医学与机械语域。

items.en: Sociology extends immobility to class structure, speaking of upward and social immobility.
items.cn: 现代社会学术语把 immobility 用于阶层结构，构成 upward immobility 与 social immobility 等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the movable stem mov-, mob-; the near-meaning group gathers words for standing still and for unchanged things.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「移动」词干 mov-、mob- 构成的一族词；近义组收表示静止不动与一成不变的说法。

normalIntro.en: Immobility is the state noun of the negative of mobile: in- takes away movement, -ity holds the state still.
normalIntro.cn: immobility 是 mobile 否定形式的「状态名词」：in- 拿走「动」，-ity 把「不动」定成一个状态。

normal.en: Im- marks the negative on m- words, while -ity names the state.
normal.cn: 在以 m 开头的词前，前缀 im- 表否定，-ity 表示一种状态。

normal.en: Prolonged immobility weakens muscles and makes recovery slower.
normal.cn: 长期不活动会让肌肉变弱，使康复变慢。

normal.en: Social immobility is the opposite of social mobility.
normal.cn: social immobility（阶层固化）正是 social mobility（社会流动）的反面。

normal.en: The verb immobilize puts something into this state.
normal.cn: 动词 immobilize 是把某物带入 immobility 这个状态。

normal.en: Compare mobile: one root, two directions, movement and its absence.
normal.cn: 对比 mobile：同一词根两个方向，一个表示能动，一个表示不能动。

abstract.en: Picture a statue of a runner, frozen in the starting pose forever.
abstract.cn: 想象一尊跑步者的雕像，永远定格在起跑姿势。

abstract.en: Think of a fly stuck in amber, motionless inside hard glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一只困在琥珀里的苍蝇，在硬玻璃般的树脂里纹丝不动。

abstract.en: See the elevator button at a fixed floor, refusing to light up after it is pressed.
abstract.cn: 想象楼层的电梯按钮一直固定不动，按下去也毫无反应。

examples.en: Prolonged immobility after surgery increases the risk of blood clots.
examples.cn: 术后长期不活动会增加血栓风险。

examples.en: Low wages and poor schools together explain the region s social immobility.
examples.cn: 低工资与差学校共同解释了这一地区的社会阶层固化。

examples.en: The physiotherapist helped him overcome months of immobility.
examples.cn: 理疗师帮助他摆脱了长达数月的行动不便。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「姨莫比力体」——姨妈力气用尽，没法比着力，一动不动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 movere（移动）→ mobilis（可移动的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 得 immobilitas → 法语 immobilite → 英语 immobility，核心义「不能动的状态」。

sensesIntro.en: Immobility begins with a body that cannot move, spreads to any still object, and then climbs to society and to anything fixed.
sensesIntro.cn: immobility 从「身体动不了」出发，扩展到任何静止的东西，再上升到社会层面与一切固定不变的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet turned to stone, unable to take the next step.
core.cn: 核心意象：双脚化成石头，迈不出下一步。

branches.en: A body that cannot move is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 身体动不了，是最字面的义项。

branches.en: Traffic, water or a machine that stalls shares the same stillness.
branches.cn: 停摆的车流、水和机器共享同一份静止。

branches.en: A frozen ladder of class is social immobility.
branches.cn: 冻结的社会阶梯，就是社会固化。

branches.en: Rules, prices or capital that cannot be shifted are fixed in place.
branches.cn: 规则、价格或资本调动不了，就是固定不变。

branches.en: Both the injured body and the stalled engine are simply unable to move.
branches.cn: 受伤的身体与停转的引擎，都是单纯地动不了。

intro.en: Immobility is built from the negating prefix in-, the Latin stem mobilis, and the state suffix -ity, all of which keep their shape in the word family.
intro.cn: immobility 由否定前缀 in-、拉丁词干 mobilis 与状态后缀 -ity 拼成，这几种成分在词族里保持原形。

latinIntro.en: Latin movere to move gives mobilis movable and immobilitas that which cannot be moved.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 movere 意为移动，派生出 mobilis（可动的）与 immobilitas（不可动的状态）。

definition_zh: 不可改变的；永恒不变的；不容更改的
definition_en: never changing, or not able to be changed
core_image: 石头刻成的律法：风吹雨打，字迹一丝不改
scene: 古人把最要紧的法律刻在铜板上，立在广场中央，任何人都不许改动。The bronze tablet carried the tribes laws, which the elders declared immutable.
sceneCN: 这里 immutable 是「不可更改的」（第 1 个义项：任何力量都改不动）；句意：铜板上刻着部落的法律，长老们宣布它永恒不变。

pos.zh: 不可改变的；永恒不变的
不容更改的；不可撤销的（规则、决定）

derivatives.zh: immutable 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「不可改变性；永恒不变」
immutable 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不可改变地」
去掉否定前缀 in- 后的正面形式，义为「可变的；易变的」
同根动词，来自拉丁 mutare，义为「改变；突变」

senses.title: Never changing
senses.definition: existing in exactly the same form and never changing at any time
senses.definitionCN: 始终以同一形态存在，任何时候都不改变
senses.example: Some of the laws of physics are regarded as immutable.
senses.exampleCN: 一些物理定律被认为永恒不变。
senses.why: The Latin negative in- denies the power to change that mutare expresses, so the word marks something change has never touched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 in- 否定了 mutare「改变」的能力，因此这个词标记的是从未被改变触碰过的东西，画面是刻好就再也不动的字。

senses.title: Not allowed to be changed
senses.definition: fixed by authority or design in such a way that no one is permitted to alter it
senses.definitionCN: 由权威或规定固定下来，谁都不准修改
senses.example: The council decided that the exchange rates were immutable for the year.
senses.exampleCN: 理事会决定，汇率在这一年内不容更改。
senses.why: Something that cannot change by nature can also be something that must not change by rule, so the word moves from physics to law.
senses.whyCN: 「本性上改不了」的东西，也可以是「按规定不许改」的东西，于是词义从自然规律延伸到法律与规章。

senses.title: In computing, unable to be altered
senses.definition: describing data or an object that cannot be changed after it has been created, so a new copy must be made instead
senses.definitionCN: 指数据或对象创建后不能再被修改，需要改动时必须另造一份新副本
senses.example: Strings in that language are immutable, so every change makes a new string.
senses.exampleCN: 那种语言里的字符串是不可变的，所以每次改动都会生成新字符串。
senses.why: The modern sense extends the physical image into a rule: once written, the value stands like engraved stone and cannot be edited in place.
senses.whyCN: 现代义项把那幅石头画面搬进数据世界：值一旦写下就像刻好的字，不能在原处涂改，只能另刻一块。

intro.en: Immutable is built on the Latin verb mutare, to change, with the negating prefix in- and the suffix -able; Latin already had the adjective immutabilis.
intro.cn: immutable 建立在拉丁动词 mutare（改变）之上，加否定前缀 in- 与后缀 -able 构成；拉丁语中本就有形容词 immutabilis。

items.en: Mutare means to change or exchange, and its adjective mutabilis means changeable.
items.cn: 拉丁语 mutare 意为改变、交换，其形容词 mutabilis 意为「可变的」。

items.en: Immutabilis adds the negative in- and states that which cannot be changed.
items.cn: immutabilis 加否定前缀 in-，表示「不可改变的」。

items.en: French immuable carries the adjective forward in a shortened form.
items.cn: 法语 immuable 以缩短的形式把该形容词传下去。

items.en: Immutable first appears in English; the deeper origin of Latin mutare is uncertain and any pre-Latin root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: immutable 于十五世纪首见于英语；拉丁 mutare 更早的来源不确定，任何拉丁语之前的词根均属重构形式。

items.en: Theology makes immutable a word for divine laws and eternal truths.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，神学用 immutable 形容神律与永恒真理。

items.en: Computing adopts the word for values that cannot be modified once created.
items.cn: 现代英语的计算领域借这个词描述创建后不可修改的值。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the change root mutare; the near-meaning group gathers words for things that do not or cannot change.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「改变」词根 mutare 构成的一族词；近义组收表示不会改变或无法改变的说法。

normalIntro.en: Immutable is the negative of mutable, and both stand on the change root mutare.
normalIntro.cn: immutable 是 mutable 的否定形式，两者都站在「改变」词根 mutare 上。

normal.en: Mut means change: mutate, mutation, mutable and immutable share it.
normal.cn: 词根 mut 表示改变：mutate、mutation、mutable、immutable 都共享它。

normal.en: In- before m- marks the negative, while -able says able to be.
normal.cn: 在以 m 开头的词前，前缀 in- 表否定，-able 表示「能被……的」。

normal.en: The noun form is immutability, the quality of never changing.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 immutability，指「不可改变」的性质。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with immune, which belongs to a different Latin root.
normal.cn: 不要与 immune 混淆，后者来自另一个拉丁词根。

normal.en: Physics speaks of immutable laws, though careful scientists avoid the word.
normal.cn: 物理学常说「不可改变的定律」，但严谨的科学家往往会避开这个说法。

abstract.en: Picture words carved deep in stone, unchanged after a thousand years of rain.
abstract.cn: 想象刻得很深的字，千年雨打仍然不变。

abstract.en: Imagine a clock whose hands are welded in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一座指针被焊死的钟。

abstract.en: Think of a legal seal pressed into hot wax and cooled hard.
abstract.cn: 想象印章按进滚烫的蜡里，冷却后坚如石头。

examples.en: The constitution sets out a few immutable principles for the courts.
examples.cn: 宪法为法院确立了几条不可更改的原则。

examples.en: Nothing in science is truly immutable, since any theory may be revised.
examples.cn: 科学中没有任何东西真正不可改变，因为任何理论都可能被修正。

examples.en: Her loyalty to the village seemed immutable.
examples.cn: 她对村庄的忠诚似乎是不会改变的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「姨谬特薄」——姨妈被谬论特薄地刻在石上，一字不许改，于是不可改变；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 mutare（改变）→ mutabilis（可变的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 得 immutabilis → 法语 immuable → 英语 immutable，核心义「改不动」。

sensesIntro.en: Immutable starts as a description of things that never change by nature, is then applied to rules that may not change, and ends as a computing label for values that cannot be edited.
sensesIntro.cn: immutable 先是形容本性上永不改变的事物，再用于「按规定不许改」的规则，最后成为计算领域里「值不可编辑」的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a law cut into stone that no hand may rework.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻进石头里的法律，谁也不能改写。

branches.en: A thing that never changes is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 永不改变的事物是基础义项。

branches.en: A rule no one may alter is the institutional sense.
branches.cn: 谁都不许改的规则是制度义项。

branches.en: A value that cannot be edited is the computing sense.
branches.cn: 无法编辑的值是计算领域的义项。

branches.en: Both natural and legal fixity share the image of engraving.
branches.cn: 自然的不变与法律的不变，共享「刻石」这同一幅画面。

branches.en: A sealed  rule and a read-only value both resist alteration.
branches.cn: 封死的规则与只读的值，都同样抗拒改动。

intro.en: Immutable combines the negative prefix in-, the change root mutare, and the suffix -able, and the same parts recur in mutable, mutation and mutate.
intro.cn: immutable 由否定前缀 in-、改变词根 mutare 与后缀 -able 组合而成，相同的成分也出现在 mutable、mutation、mutate 里。

latinIntro.en: Latin mutare to change gives mutabilis changeable and immutabilis unchangeable; the deeper origin of mutare is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mutare 意为改变，派生出 mutabilis（可变的）与 immutabilis（不可变的）；mutare 更早的来源不确定。

definition_zh: 损害；削弱；使变差；（医学）使功能受损
definition_en: to damage or weaken something so that it works less well than before
core_image: 好端端的齿轮被磨掉一角：还能转，却转得不顺
scene: 夜里连续熬夜赶工，第二天说话都变得磕磕绊绊。Too little sleep impaired his concentration during the exam.
sceneCN: 这里 impair 是「削弱、损害」（第 1 个义项：使能力或功能变差）；句意：睡眠太少，损害了他在考试中的注意力。

pos.zh: 使（身体或感官功能）受损（医学用法）

derivatives.zh: impair 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「损害；损伤；机能障碍」
过去分词作形容词，义为「受损的；有障碍的」，如 hearing impaired
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「未受损的；完好无损的」
加施事后缀 -er 构成，义为「造成损害的人或物」，较少使用

senses.title: To weaken the quality or function
senses.definition: to make something such as judgement, performance or a sense work less well than it should
senses.definitionCN: 使判断力、表现或感官等本可正常发挥的功能不如原本那样好
senses.example: Loud music can impair concentration in a reading room.
senses.exampleCN: 吵闹的音乐会削弱阅览室里的注意力。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to make worse, and English keeps that gradient: nothing is destroyed, but the quality slips a grade.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「弄得更糟」，英语保留了这种「降一档」的分寸：东西并没有被毁掉，只是质量掉了一个等级，像齿轮被磨掉一角还照转。

senses.title: To damage health or a body part
senses.definition: to damage a part of the body or a bodily function, often gradually and sometimes permanently
senses.definitionCN: 损伤身体某一部分或某项身体功能，往往是逐渐发生的，并且可能成为永久性损伤
senses.example: Years of noise at the factory had impaired his hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 多年工厂噪音已经损伤了他的听力。
senses.why: If a function can drop a grade, repeated wear can make the drop permanent, so medicine uses the word for damaged sight, hearing or movement.
senses.whyCN: 功能既然会掉一档，日积月累的磨损就可能让这一档永远补不回来，于是医学用这个词指视力、听力或运动功能受损。

senses.title: In law, to reduce a right or value
senses.definition: in legal writing, to harm a right, a claim or a value so that it is worth less than before
senses.definitionCN: 法律文书中，损害一项权利、主张或价值，使其效力或价值低于原来
senses.example: The new clause could impair the rights of existing tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新条款可能损害现有租户的权利。
senses.why: Law borrows the image of value made worse: a right that has been impaired still exists, but it no longer carries its full force.
senses.whyCN: 法律借用了「价值被弄差」的画面：被 impair 的权利依然存在，只是不再保有如初的效力，与彻底无效不同。

intro.en: Impair comes from Old French empeirier, itself from late Latin impejorare, built on pejor, worse; the English form took on the im- spelling in the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: impair 来自古法语 empeirier，再往前是晚期拉丁语 impejorare，建立在 pejor（更坏的）之上；英语形式在十五世纪形成了 im- 拼写。

items.en: Pejor means worse, the comparative of malus, bad, and gives the whole word its sense of making things worse.
items.cn: pejor 意为「更坏的」，是 malus（坏的）的比较级，正是这个比较级给了整个词「弄得更糟」的意思。

items.en: Impejorare, with the prefix in-, means to make worse or damage.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 impejorare 带前缀 in-，意为「弄得更糟；损害」。

items.en: Empeirier carries the verb into French, where the sound shifts in the direction of impair.
items.cn: 法语 empeirier 把这一动词传承下来，其后读音朝 impair 的方向变化。

items.en: English uses forms such as empeyre and ampayre before settling on impair.
items.cn: 英语先出现 empeyre、ampayre 一类拼写，之后才稳定为 impair。

items.en: The word spreads from general harm to health, hearing and legal rights.
items.cn: 这个词从一般性的「伤害」扩展到健康、听力与法律权利等语境。

items.en: The participle impaired becomes a standard neutral adjective in phrases such as visually impaired.
items.cn: 分词 impaired 成为标准的中性形容词，用于 visually impaired（视力有障碍）等说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the same worse root pejor and on the im- spelling; the near-meaning group gathers verbs for harming and weakening that differ in strength.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「更坏」词根 pejor 的词以及 im- 拼写的近邻词；近义组收表示伤害与削弱的动词，强度各不相同。

entries.definition: damage to a function or ability
entries.definitionCN: 损害；机能障碍

entries.definition: damaged or weakened
entries.definitionCN: 受损的；有障碍的

entries.definition: expressing disapproval; from the same Latin pejor, worse
entries.definitionCN: 贬损的；来自同一拉丁词 pejor（更坏的）

entries.definition: to hurt or damage someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 伤害；损害（最宽泛，可指任何伤害）

entries.definition: to make someone or something less strong
entries.definitionCN: 削弱；使变弱

entries.definition: to gradually weaken something from below, especially confidence or authority
entries.definitionCN: 暗中削弱；动摇（多指慢慢侵蚀信心或权威）

normalIntro.en: Impair is the verb for making something worse: the root pejor means worse, and English pairs it with the prefix im-.
normalIntro.cn: impair 是表示「弄得更糟」的动词：词根 pejor 意为更坏的，英语再配上前缀 im-。

normal.en: Pejor means worse in Latin and also lies behind pejorative.
normal.cn: pejor 在拉丁语中意为更坏的，也是 pejorative（贬损的）的词根。

normal.en: The noun is impairment, as in visual impairment or hearing impairment.
normal.cn: 名词是 impairment，例如 visual impairment（视力障碍）与 hearing impairment（听力障碍）。

normal.en: The participle impaired works as a neutral adjective after an adverb: visually impaired, mentally impaired.
normal.cn: 分词 impaired 常跟副词作中性形容词：visually impaired（视障）、mentally impaired（精神受损）。

normal.en: Impair is milder than destroy: the thing still works, only less well.
normal.cn: impair 比 destroy 弱：东西还在用，只是效果变差了。

normal.en: Alcohol impairs judgement before it impairs walking.
normal.cn: 酒精先损害判断力，然后才影响走路。

abstract.en: Picture a cog with one corner worn away, still turning with a rattle.
abstract.cn: 想象一个被磨掉一角的齿轮，还能转，却咔哒作响。

abstract.en: Imagine a window slowly clouded by steam, still showing the street but dimly.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇被水汽慢慢蒙住的窗，街道还看得见，却模糊了。

abstract.en: Think of a runner whose ankle is taped: the race goes on, but slower.
abstract.cn: 想象一名脚踝缠上绷带的跑者：比赛照跑，只是慢了。

examples.en: Air pollution can impair lung function in young children.
examples.cn: 空气污染会损害幼儿的肺功能。

examples.en: His vision was permanently impaired by the accident.
examples.cn: 那场事故让他的视力永久受损。

examples.en: The court ruled that the clause impaired the rights of tenants.
examples.cn: 法院裁定该条款损害了租户的权利。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一摸皮儿」——摸一下皮儿就掉了，东西被弄坏了；这是拆字谐音联想，与真实词源（拉丁 pejor，更坏）无关。

root: 拉丁语 pejor（更坏的，malus 的比较级）→ 晚期拉丁 impejorare（弄得更糟）→ 古法语 empeirier → 中古英语 empeyre → 现代英语 impair；词根在拉丁语之外的更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Impair starts from a general sense of making a quality worse, narrows onto damaged health and senses, and widens again in law to rights and values.
sensesIntro.cn: impair 从泛指「使质量变差」出发，收窄到健康与感官受损，再在法律语境中扩展到权利与价值减损。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a good mechanism with one corner worn away.
core.cn: 核心意象：完好的机件被磨掉一角。

branches.en: Making judgement or performance less good is the general sense.
branches.cn: 让判断力或表现变差，是一般义项。

branches.en: Damaged hearing or sight is the medical sense.
branches.cn: 听力或视力受损，是医学义项。

branches.en: A reduced right is the legal sense.
branches.cn: 被减损的权利，是法律义项。

branches.en: A weakened mind and a damaged ear both lose working ability.
branches.cn: 被削弱的头脑与受损的耳朵，都失去了部分工作能力。

branches.en: Both a body function and a legal claim can be left impaired but not destroyed.
branches.cn: 身体功能与法律主张都可能处于受损却未被彻底取消的状态。

intro.en: Impair is built from the Latin comparative pejor, worse, and the prefix im-, with impairment and impaired carrying the family in modern English.
intro.cn: impair 由拉丁语比较级 pejor（更坏的）与前缀 im- 构成，现代英语靠 impairment 与 impaired 延续这一族。

latinIntro.en: Latin pejor, worse, gives the late verb impejorare to make worse, which French shortened into empeirier.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pejor（更坏的）先派生出晚期动词 impejorare（弄得更糟），法语再把它缩短为 empeirier。

items.meaning: into, toward; here a hardened form of in-
items.meaningCN: 进入、朝向；此处是 in- 的强化形态
items.example: impair, impeach
items.exampleCN: 损害；弹劾

items.example: Pejor gives impair and pejorative.
items.exampleCN: pejor 构成 impair 与 pejorative。

items.example: impejorare, validate
items.exampleCN: 使更坏；使有效

items.example: Impejorare is the direct ancestor of impair.
items.exampleCN: impejorare 是 impair 的直接祖先。

items.meaning: result or state of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示行为结果或状态的名词后缀
items.example: impairment, movement
items.exampleCN: 损害；移动

items.meaningCN: 过去分词与形容词词尾
items.example: impaired, exhausted
items.exampleCN: 受损的；精疲力竭的

items.example: unimpaired, unaffected
items.exampleCN: 未受损的；未受影响的

items.meaningCN: 表示施动者的名词后缀
items.example: impairer, adviser
items.exampleCN: 造成损害者；顾问

items.example: A pejorative label can hurt.
items.exampleCN: 一个贬损性的标签可能伤人。

items.example: She has a mild hearing impairment.
items.exampleCN: 她有轻度听力障碍。

definition_zh: 传授；告知；透露；赋予；给予（某种特质）
definition_en: to give or pass on knowledge, information, a feeling or a quality to someone else
core_image: 一位老师把手里的一卷东西递到学生摊开的手心里
scene: 大学讲堂里，老教授俯身把毕生的研究心得讲给学生。Over the years the old professor managed to impart his love of chemistry to every student who entered his lab.
sceneCN: 这里 impart 是「传授（知识、经验）」（第 1 个义项：把学问教给他人）；句意为多年来这位老教授成功地把对化学的热爱传给了他实验室里的每个学生。中文铺垫不含数字，英文句只出现一次目标词。

collocations.zh: 赋予……的感觉；让人产生……感

derivatives.zh: 由 impart 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「传授；给予」
impart 去掉前缀后剩下的 core 部分，义为「部分；一份」，与 impart 共享「分出一份」的拉丁词根
由词根 part 加 -ible 构成，义为「可分的」；注意它并非由 impart 派生，而是表示「可以分割的」

senses.title: To pass knowledge or skills on to someone
senses.definition: to teach someone knowledge, skills or values by passing them from one side to the other
senses.definitionCN: 把知识、技能或价值观教给他人，使其成为对方的东西
senses.example: Good teachers impart more than facts; they teach students how to think.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师传授的不只是事实，而是教学生如何思考。
senses.why: The Latin verb impartire is split into a share, so teaching is pictured as handing a portion of what you have to someone else.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词本义是「分出一份」，所以传授被设想为把自己拥有的一份交到别人手上。

senses.title: To make information known
senses.definition: to tell people information, news or a message in a formal or gentle way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或委婉的方式把信息、消息告知他人
senses.example: The doctor imparted the bad news as gently as she could.
senses.exampleCN: 医生尽可能温和地把坏消息告诉了病人。
senses.why: If knowledge can be handed over, news can be handed over too, so the same verb covers telling people something.
senses.whyCN: 既然知识可以「递交」出去，消息同样可以交到别人手上，于是同一个动词也用来表示告知。

senses.title: To give a quality to something
senses.definition: to give a particular quality, taste or feeling to an object or a place
senses.definitionCN: 赋予某物或某地某种性质、味道或感觉
senses.example: A few herbs will impart a rich flavour to the soup.
senses.exampleCN: 加几味香草，汤的味道就会变得浓郁丰富。
senses.why: When a quality is added to a thing, it seems to be handed into that thing, which extends the share-giving image to taste and atmosphere.
senses.whyCN: 把某种性质加进事物里，就像把它递进那件事物中，于是「分出一份」的意象扩展到了味道与氛围。

senses.title: To share a feeling with others
senses.definition: to make other people feel an emotion or an atmosphere that you have
senses.definitionCN: 让其他人感受到你所拥有的情绪或气氛
senses.example: Her calm voice imparted a sense of safety to the frightened children.
senses.exampleCN: 她平静的声音让受惊的孩子们感到安心。
senses.why: Emotions spread from person to person, and the hand-to-hand image fits the way a good mood is passed along.
senses.whyCN: 情绪会在人之间蔓延，「手递手」的画面正好贴合好心情如何被传下去。

senses.title: To transmit something at a distance
senses.definition: to transmit light, colour or heat from one thing to another
senses.definitionCN: 把光、颜色或热量从一处传导到另一处
senses.example: Glass windows impart no colour of their own but borrow light from the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 玻璃窗本身没有颜色，只是把天空的光借进来。
senses.why: In older use, light and colour were described as being handed from an object to the eye, an extension of the giving image.
senses.whyCN: 早期用法中，光和颜色被说成从物体递到眼睛里，这是「给予」意象的延伸。

senses.title: To give a right or property to someone
senses.definition: to give a legal right or a share of property to another person
senses.definitionCN: 把某项合法权利或某份财产分给他人
senses.example: The will imparted a quarter of the land to each of the four grandchildren.
senses.exampleCN: 遗嘱把四分之一土地分别给了四个孙辈。
senses.why: This is the oldest legal layer: impartire meant to allocate a share, and law still speaks of rights and land being imparted.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的法律层次：词根本义是「分配一份」，法律至今仍说权利与土地被授予。

senses.title: To disclose a secret
senses.definition: to reveal private or secret information to someone who did not know it
senses.definitionCN: 把私密的或秘密的信息透露给原先不知情的人
senses.example: He would not impart the details of the meeting to the press.
senses.exampleCN: 他不愿把会议的细节透露给媒体。
senses.why: Hidden information is like a wrapped parcel, and imparting it is opening the parcel and placing it in another person hands.
senses.whyCN: 隐藏的信息像一个包好的包裹，透露就是打开包裹把它放进别人手里。

senses.title: To add a hint of something
senses.definition: to add a slight touch of a colour, mood or tone to something
senses.definitionCN: 给某物添上一丝颜色、情绪或格调
senses.example: Oak barrels impart a faint vanilla taste to the wine.
senses.exampleCN: 橡木桶给葡萄酒添上一丝淡淡的香草味。
senses.why: Even a very small share can be handed out, so the verb covers a faint touch added to colour or mood.
senses.whyCN: 哪怕一份很小的份额也能分出去，所以这个词也指给颜色或情绪添上的一丝痕迹。

intro.en: Impart comes from Latin impartire (also impertere), built from in- plus partire, to divide, which descends from pars, a part.
intro.cn: impart 来自拉丁语 impartire（亦作 impertere），由 in- 加 partire（分割）构成，而 partire 源自 pars（部分）。

items.en: The reconstructed root per- meant to allot or assign, and it underlies Latin pars and many modern words for parts.
items.cn: 重构词根 per- 意为「分配、划归」，它是拉丁语 pars 以及许多现代「部分」类词的来源。

items.en: Pars means a part or a share, and partirishare grows from it; the family already carries the idea of dividing.
items.cn: pars 意为部分、一份，partiri（分割）由此生长出来，这个词族一开始就带着「切分」的意思。

items.en: Impertire and impartire add in- (into) to the dividing verb, giving the sense of distributing a share into someone hands.
items.cn: impertire 与 impartire 给「分割」动词加上 in-（进入），形成「把一份分到某人手中」的意思。

items.en: The Latin verb reaches Old French as impartir, with the legal and teaching senses already in place.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词进入古法语成为 impartir，法律与教学两层含义都已具备。

items.en: Impart first appears in English in the fifteenth century, mainly in legal prose about rights and property.
items.cn: impart 在十五世纪首次出现于英语，主要见于关于权利与财产的律令文字。

items.en: Over time the verb widens from legal shares to knowledge, news, feeling, flavour and a faint tint.
items.cn: 此后这个词从法律上的份额扩展到知识、消息、情感、风味与一丝色调。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin part root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs that give knowledge, news or qualities, with different strength and formality.
note.cn: 形近组收以拉丁语 part 词根构成的一族词；近义组收「给予知识、消息或性质」的动词，力度与正式程度各不相同。

entries.definition: A portion of a whole, or one of the divisions of something; the base of the Latin root that impart contains.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「部分、一份」，是 impart 所含拉丁词根的基础形态。

entries.definition: A share of something given to a person, from the same Latin root as a part of a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「一份、份额」，与「部分」同出拉丁词根。

entries.definition: To take a share in something such as food or an activity; it looks like impart but comes from part plus take.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「参与、共享」，如一起分享食物或活动；看似与 impart 相像，其实由 part 加 take 构成。

entries.definition: To make an idea or feeling understood by others; wider than impart and common for messages.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「传达、表达想法或感受」，比 impart 范围更宽，常用于传递讯息。

entries.definition: To send information, signals or diseases from one place to another; technical and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「发送、传输信息、信号或疾病」，较为技术性且中性。

entries.definition: To give an honour or gift formally; more pompous than impart and mostly used for awards.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「授予荣誉或礼物」，语气比 impart 更隆重，多用于颁奖。

normalIntro.en: Impart keeps the in- plus part shape: you take a part of what you know and put it into someone else.
normalIntro.cn: impart 保留 in- 加 part 的形状：你拿出自己知道的一部分，放进别人那里。

normal.en: The word splits into im- plus part, and a teacher gives a part of the lesson to each student.
normal.cn: 这个词可以拆成 im- 加 part，老师把课程的一份份交给每个学生。

normal.en: The common pattern is a verb plus something plus to plus a person, with the receiver at the end.
normal.cn: 常见结构是动词后加给予之物、再加介词 to 和接受者，接受者出现在句末。

normal.en: Knowledge, information and a sense of something are the standard things imparted.
normal.cn: 知识、信息与某种感觉是 impart 最常接的宾语。

normal.en: Impartation is the noun; impartible means divisible and is built from part, not from impart.
normal.cn: impartation 是名词；impartible 意为「可分的」，由 part 构成而非由 impart 派生。

normal.en: Compared with teach, impart points at what the speaker holds and hands over, not at the learner.
normal.cn: 与 teach 相比，impart 着眼于说话者拥有并交出去的东西，而不是学习者。

abstract.en: A hand passes a folded note into another open hand, and both hands are still touching.
abstract.cn: 一只手把折好的纸条递到另一只摊开的手里，两只手还停在一起。

abstract.en: A chef pours one spoonful of a private stock into another cook pot.
abstract.cn: 一位厨师把自己的一勺私藏高汤倒进另一口锅里。

abstract.en: A smell drifts through an open door and quietly changes the mood of the next room.
abstract.cn: 一缕气味穿过敞开的门，悄悄改变了隔壁房间的气氛。

examples.en: Parents want teachers to impart good study habits, not just answers.
examples.cn: 家长希望老师传授好的学习习惯，而不只是答案。

examples.en: The officer was required to impart the decision to the families in person.
examples.cn: 这名官员被要求亲自把决定告知家属。

examples.en: A pinch of saffron will impart a golden colour to the rice.
examples.cn: 一小撮藏红花会给米饭染上一层金黄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「衣姆怕特」——把外衣的一角分给怕冷的朋友，就是「给予一份」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pars（部分）→ partiri（分割）→ impertire / impartire（分配一份、给予）→ 古法语 impartir → 英语 impart。核心义从「分出一份」演化为「传授、告知、赋予」。

sensesIntro.en: Impart starts from a legal sense of handing over a share and spreads outward to knowledge, news, feelings, flavours and faint touches of colour.
sensesIntro.cn: impart 从法律上「交出一份」的含义出发，向外扩展到知识、消息、情感、风味以及一丝颜色的意味。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand passing a share of something into another open hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把一份东西递到另一只摊开的手里。

branches.en: Teaching and telling are the two most common everyday branches.
branches.cn: 传授与告知是日常最常见的两个分支。

branches.en: Taste, mood and a faint tint are qualities handed into a thing.
branches.cn: 味道、气氛与一丝色调都是被递给事物的性质。

branches.en: The legal branch keeps the original sense of allocating a share.
branches.cn: 法律分支保留「分配份额」的本义。

branches.en: The transmission branch treats light and heat as things passed between objects.
branches.cn: 传导分支把光与热当作在物体之间传递的东西。

branches.en: Disclosing a secret is handing over hidden information.
branches.cn: 透露秘密就是把隐藏的信息交出去。

intro.en: Impart is a Latin verb split into in- plus part-, with in- marking direction and the part root marking a share.
intro.cn: impart 是一个可以拆成 in- 加 part- 的拉丁动词，in- 表示方向，part 词根表示一份。

latinIntro.en: The Latin elements are in-, meaning into, and partire and pars, meaning to divide and a part.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁成分是表示「进入」的 in-，以及表示「分割」的 partire 与表示「部分」的 pars。

items.example: The prefix points the giving hand towards the receiver.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「给予」的手势指向接受者。

items.example: Before p, in- often turns into im-, as in impartere.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，in- 常变为 im-，如 impartere。

items.example: The root part- carries the idea of a portion being divided.
items.exampleCN: 词根 part- 带着「被切分的一份」的意思。

items.example: Pars is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pars 是整族词的源头。

items.example: Partire supplies the dividing action.
items.exampleCN: partire 提供「分割」这个动作。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms impartation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 构成 impartation。

items.example: Impartation keeps the teaching sense as a noun.
items.exampleCN: impartation 以名词形式保留教学含义。

items.example: The past form imparted marks a finished act of giving.
items.exampleCN: 过去式 imparted 标记已经完成的给予动作。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms impartible, from a different starting point.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 impartible，其构词起点不同。

latinEntries.example: Partire is the dividing verb at the centre.
latinEntries.exampleCN: partire 是位于中心的分割动词。

latinEntries.example: Impertire is an older spelling of the same verb.
latinEntries.exampleCN: impertire 是同一动词的较早拼法。

derivatives.zh: 传授；给予
被传授的；被给予的

definition_zh: 冷漠的；无动于衷的；不动声色的；面不改色的
definition_en: not showing any emotion, especially when strong feelings would be expected
core_image: 一张毫无表情的脸，像一尊石雕，任凭风吹雨打也不动容
scene: 审判结束后记者围住证人追问，证人的脸却没有任何起伏。Even when the verdict was read out, the accused man remained impassive.
sceneCN: 这里 impassive 是「毫无表情的、不动声色的」（第 2 个义项：不流露任何情绪）；句意为即使宣读判决结果时，被告依然面无表情。

pos.zh: 形容词：冷漠的；无动于衷的；不露声色的

derivatives.zh: 由 impassive 替换词尾为 -ity 构成，义为「冷漠；不动声色」
由 impassive 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不动声色地」
由 impassive 加 -ness 构成，义为「无动于衷的状态」

senses.title: Lacking the capacity to feel or suffer
senses.definition: having no feeling and no capacity to suffer pain, as a stone or a corpse
senses.definitionCN: 没有感觉，也不会有痛苦，如同石头或尸体
senses.example: The carved face of the statue is impassive and cannot feel the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 雕像那张雕刻出来的脸毫无感觉，也感受不到雨。
senses.why: In- means not and the Latin root pati means to suffer, so impassive first describes what cannot feel anything at all.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「不」，拉丁词根 pati 表示「承受痛苦」，所以这个词最早形容那些根本感受不到任何东西的事物。

senses.title: Showing no emotion on the face
senses.titleCN: 面无表情的；不动声色的
senses.definition: not showing any emotion in the face or voice, often when feeling is expected
senses.definitionCN: 在脸上或声音里不流露出任何情绪，尤其是在别人期待他有所反应时
senses.example: She kept her face impassive while the manager scolded her.
senses.exampleCN: 经理训斥她时，她始终面无表情。
senses.why: When nothing can pass into a feeling, nothing shows on the surface either, so the root image moves from having no feeling to showing none.
senses.whyCN: 若感觉无法进入内心，表面自然也不会有任何流露，于是词根意象从「没有感觉」转到了「不表现出来」。

senses.title: Calm and unmoved by bad news
senses.definition: staying calm and collected when something alarming or painful happens
senses.definitionCN: 在发生令人惊恐或痛苦的事情时仍然保持冷静沉着
senses.example: The nurse gave the news in an impassive voice so as not to alarm the family.
senses.exampleCN: 护士用平静的语气说出这个消息，以免惊动家属。
senses.why: A person who is not moved by events seems to stand outside the wave of feeling, which makes the word a compliment for calmness.
senses.whyCN: 不被事件撼动的人仿佛站在情绪浪潮之外，因此这个词也用来称赞人的冷静。

senses.title: Indifferent or careless about others
senses.definition: seeming not to care about someone else suffering or about what happens
senses.definitionCN: 似乎不在乎他人遭受的痛苦或所发生的事情
senses.example: The crowd stood impassive while the old man struggled to his feet.
senses.exampleCN: 老人挣扎着站起来时，人群却无动于衷。
senses.why: If no feeling reaches a person, that person can look cold to those who do feel pain, so the word also carries the charge of indifference.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有任何感受能够进入一个人内心，对那些真正感受痛苦的人来说他就显得冷冰冰，因此这个词也带上了冷漠的色彩。

senses.title: Neutral in face or tone
senses.definition: showing a fair and controlled face or tone that reveals no opinion
senses.definitionCN: 表现出公正而克制的表情或语气，不泄露任何倾向
senses.example: The judge listened to both lawyers with an impassive expression.
senses.exampleCN: 法官以不带倾向的表情听完了双方律师的陈述。
senses.why: A face that gives nothing away can be read as fair, which is why the word suits judges and moderators.
senses.whyCN: 一张不透露任何信息的脸容易被看作公正，因此这个词也常用来形容法官与主持人。

senses.title: Frozen and lifeless in appearance
senses.definition: looking stiff, blank or lifeless, as if it were carved rather than living
senses.definitionCN: 看上去僵硬、空洞、没有生气，仿佛雕出来的而不是活生生的
senses.example: His impassive features made it hard to tell whether he was joking.
senses.exampleCN: 他那张呆板的脸让人很难判断他是不是在开玩笑。
senses.why: The stone image of the root shows again when a real face becomes so still that it looks unnaturally hard.
senses.whyCN: 当一张真实的脸静止得像是石头雕成的，词根里「石像」的画面就又浮现出来。

senses.title: Not easily excited or disturbed
senses.definition: having a nature that is not quickly excited, stirred or upset
senses.definitionCN: 性情沉稳，不容易被激发、撩动或扰乱
senses.example: She has an impassive temperament that helps her in emergency medicine.
senses.exampleCN: 她性情沉静，这让她在急诊医学工作中受益匪浅。
senses.why: A person who is rarely stirred by events tends to have a steady nature, so the no-feeling root shades into an untroubled temperament.
senses.whyCN: 很少被外界撩动的人往往性情稳定，于是「无感觉」的词根渐渐偏向「不易被扰动的性格」。

senses.title: Blank, showing no response at all
senses.titleCN: 毫无回应的；毫无生气的
senses.definition: showing no visible sign of response, as of an object or a system that gives no output
senses.definitionCN: 看不出任何回应的迹象，如毫无输出的物体或系统
senses.example: The screen was impassive, showing only a grey line across the top.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕毫无反应，只在顶部显示一条灰线。
senses.why: Once a surface stops reacting at all, the word reaches things that never answer back, like a silent screen.
senses.whyCN: 一旦表面完全不再作出反应，这个词就触及那些从不应答的事物，例如一块沉默的屏幕。

intro.en: Impassive is built from the negative prefix in- and passion, from Latin pati, to suffer, so it literally means not suffering.
intro.cn: impassive 由否定前缀 in- 与 passion 构成，而 passion 源自拉丁语 pati（承受、受苦），字面义就是「不受苦」。

items.en: The reconstructed root pei- means to hurt or strike, and it lies behind the Latin family for suffering.
items.cn: 重构词根 pei- 意为「伤害、打击」，是拉丁语「受苦」词族的底子。

items.en: Pati means to suffer or endure, and passio names a suffering or a strong feeling.
items.cn: pati 意为忍受、受苦，passio 则指痛苦或强烈的情感。

items.en: Through Old French the noun becomes passion, which joins in- to form impassif.
items.cn: 经由古法语，名词变成 passion，再接上 in- 构成 impassif。

items.en: Impassive enters English in the seventeenth century, first describing things that cannot feel pain.
items.cn: impassive 在十七世纪进入英语，最初形容无法感到痛苦的事物。

items.en: In the nineteenth century it shifts to people and faces, meaning not showing emotion.
items.cn: 到十九世纪它转向描写人和脸，意思是「不流露感情」。

items.en: The modern word covers the cold face, the calm official and the indifferent crowd.
items.cn: 现代英语中它覆盖了冷漠的脸、镇定的官员与无动于衷的人群。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that share the in- plus pass- shape; the near-meaning group gathers words for showing little or no feeling, each with a different tilt.
note.cn: 形近组收同样由 in- 加 pass- 构成的词；近义组收表示「很少或没有情绪流露」的词，各自侧重不同。

entries.definition: Full of strong and intense feeling; it looks like impassive but adds the suffix -ed to opposite effect.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「充满激情的、热烈的」；拼写与 impassive 相近，但词尾 -ed 带来了相反的意味。

entries.definition: Strong emotion or eager love; the noun inside impassive, now negated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「激情、热爱」，是 impassive 中被否定的那个名词。

entries.definition: The quality of showing no emotion; the abstract noun of impassive.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「面无表情、冷漠」，是 impassive 的抽象名词。

entries.definition: Showing nothing at all on the face; very close to impassive but limited to the face.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「毫无表情的」，与 impassive 很接近，但只适用于脸部。

entries.definition: Showing no expression on purpose, often for a joke; informal and humorous.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「板着脸的」，常是故意为之以求搞笑，口语化且带幽默。

entries.definition: Distant and unfriendly, not joining in with others; more about manner than face.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「疏远的、冷淡的」，更侧重待人态度而不是面部表情。

normalIntro.en: Impassive is in- plus passion: no strong feeling can come in, so nothing shows on the surface.
normalIntro.cn: impassive 就是 in- 加 passion：强烈的感情进不来，表面上也就什么也看不到。

normal.en: The word reads as im- (not) plus passion, so an impassive person shows no passion in sight.
normal.cn: 这个词可以读成 im-（不）加 passion，impassive 的人身上看不到激情。

normal.en: The two common frames are remain impassive and an impassive expression, often after bad news.
normal.cn: 两个常见框架是 remain impassive 与 an impassive expression，多出现在坏消息之后。

normal.en: Impassive and impassioned are near opposites despite the shared pass- stem.
normal.cn: impassive 与 impassioned 词干同样含 pass-，意思却几乎相反。

normal.en: Impassively is the adverb and impassivity is the noun, and both keep the -ive stem.
normal.cn: impassively 是副词，impassivity 是名词，两者都保留 -ive 词干。

normal.en: Impassive suggests control of feeling, while expressionless only says that the face shows nothing.
normal.cn: impassive 暗示对感情的克制，expressionless 只说明脸上没有表情。

abstract.en: A stone face on a temple wall with rain running down it, the features never changing.
abstract.cn: 庙墙上的一张石雕面孔，雨水顺着流下，神情丝毫不变。

abstract.en: A white swan on a still lake while the storm passes overhead.
abstract.cn: 风浪从头顶掠过时，一只白天鹅静静浮在湖面上。

abstract.en: A curtain drawn so tight that not one ray of light gets through.
abstract.cn: 一幅拉得严严实实的窗帘，透不进一丝光。

examples.en: The chairman listened to the criticism with an impassive face.
examples.cn: 董事长面无表情地听着这些批评。

examples.en: Soldiers are trained to stay impassive while civilians panic.
examples.cn: 士兵受过训练，在平民慌乱时仍要保持镇定。

examples.en: Her impassive reply gave no clue about what she really thought.
examples.cn: 她不动声色的回答完全看不出她真正的想法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬怕洗」——脸硬得像石头，什么都不怕，洗也洗不出表情来，就是「不为所动」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pati（忍受、受苦）→ passio（痛苦；强烈情感）→ 古法语 passion → 加否定前缀 in- 构成 impassif / impassive，字面义「不受苦、无感觉」，再引申为「不露感情」。

sensesIntro.en: Impassive grows from the root of suffering that is denied: not able to feel, then not showing feeling, and finally indifferent, calm or simply blank.
sensesIntro.cn: impassive 从被否定的「受苦」词根生长出来：先是无法感觉，接着是不显露感觉，最后衍生出冷漠、镇定或一片空白。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone face that no wind or rain can move.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张风吹雨打也不动的石雕面孔。

branches.en: The literal no-feeling sense lives on in stone and blank features.
branches.cn: 字面上的「无感觉」义项存留在石头与空洞的表情中。

branches.en: A face that hides emotion looks controlled and fair.
branches.cn: 藏起情绪的脸看起来既克制又公正。

branches.en: Steadiness and a calm nature come from not being moved by events.
branches.cn: 镇定与沉稳的性情来自不被外界撼动。

branches.en: Indifference is the dark side of not being reached by feeling.
branches.cn: 冷漠是「感觉无法进入」的阴暗一面。

branches.en: A surface that gives no sign at all is the far end of the same chain.
branches.cn: 毫无迹象的表面是同一条链条最远的一端。

intro.en: Impassive is a negative prefix fixed onto the Latin root for suffering and feeling.
intro.cn: impassive 就是在拉丁语「受苦、感受」的词根前否定前缀。

latinIntro.en: The skeleton is Latin in- (not) plus pati and passio, meaning to suffer and a suffering.
latinIntro.cn: 它的骨架是拉丁语否定前缀 in- 加上 pati 与 passio，二者分别表示「受苦」与「痛苦」。

items.example: The prefix turns the idea of feeling into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「有感觉」的想法翻转成反面。

items.example: Before p and b, in- becomes im-, as in impassive.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 和 b 之前，in- 变成 im-，如 impassive。

items.example: Pati is the feeling root behind passion.
items.exampleCN: pati 是 passion 背后的「感受」词根。

items.example: Passio gives English passion.
items.exampleCN: passio 衍生出英语的 passion。

items.example: The suffix -ive makes impassive an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 使 impassive 成为形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms impassively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 impassively。

items.example: Impassively answers the question how.
items.exampleCN: impassively 回答「如何」的问题。

items.example: Swapping the ending for -ity gives impassivity.
items.exampleCN: 把词尾换成 -ity 就得到 impassivity。

items.meaning: the state of showing no feeling
items.example: Impassivity names the state rather than the person.
items.exampleCN: impassivity 命名的是状态而不是人。

latinEntries.example: Pati supplies the feeling that is denied.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pati 提供被否定的「感受」。

latinEntries.example: Passus is the participle behind the pass- stem.
latinEntries.exampleCN: passus 是 pass- 词干背后的分词形式。

latinEntries.example: Passio leads to Old French passion.

冷漠；无动于衷

definition_zh: 弹劾；控告；怀疑（信誉、动机等）；质疑
definition_en: to charge someone, especially a public official, with wrongdoing, or to cast doubt on a person or a claim
core_image: 一只手指着公职人员的胸口，当众宣读他的罪名
scene: 议会大厅里，反对派领袖站起来宣读调查结论。The committee voted to impeach the minister over the misuse of public funds.
sceneCN: 这里 impeach 是「（议会）弹劾」（第 1 个义项：指控公职人员违法而启动罢免程序）；句意为委员会经投票决定以滥用公款为由弹劾该部长。

collocations.zh: 对某人的动机提出质疑

derivatives.zh: 由 impeach 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「弹劾；控告」
由 impeach 加 -able 构成，义为「可被弹劾的」
由 un- 加 impeachable 构成，义为「无可指责的、不容置疑的」

senses.title: To charge a public official with misconduct
senses.definition: to accuse a public official of serious wrongdoing, which may lead to removal from office
senses.definitionCN: 指控公职人员犯有严重过错，其结果可能导致其被免职
senses.example: The opposition tried to impeach the governor for taking bribes.
senses.exampleCN: 反对派试图以收受贿赂为由弹劾州长。
senses.why: The prefix im- means into and the Latin root for foot gives the image of something being caught in a snare, so to impeach is to put someone into a trap of legal charges.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 im- 表示「进入」，与「脚」相关的拉丁词根带来被绳网绊住的画面，所以弹劾就是把某人套进指控的网里。

senses.title: To accuse someone formally in law
senses.definition: to bring a formal charge against a person before a court or a body with power to judge
senses.definitionCN: 向法庭或有权审理的机构正式对某人提出指控
senses.example: The old law allowed any citizen to impeach a dishonest tax collector.
senses.exampleCN: 旧法允许任何公民检举不诚实的税务官。
senses.why: Before the word was limited to politics, it was a general legal verb for bringing a charge, and the snare image fits any accusation.
senses.whyCN: 在语义被限定到政治领域之前，它是一般性的法律动词，任何指控都能用那个「套网」的画面来解释。

senses.title: To cast doubt on someone or something
senses.definition: to question the truth, honesty or value of a person, a statement or a claim
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某说法或某主张的真实性、诚信或价值提出怀疑
senses.example: New evidence could impeach the testimony of the key witness.
senses.exampleCN: 新证据可能会让关键证人的证词受到质疑。
senses.why: A charge laid against a claim attacks its credit, so the legal verb extends to any attack on trust.
senses.whyCN: 对一种说法提出指控就是攻击它的信誉，于是这个法律动词扩展到了任何对信任的冲击。

senses.title: To challenge the credibility of a witness
senses.definition: to attack the reliability of a witness in court by pointing out mistakes or bias
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上通过指出错误或偏见来攻击证人证词的可靠性
senses.example: The defence lawyer tried to impeach the witness with a previous lie.
senses.exampleCN: 辩护律师试图用证人从前的一次说谎来质疑其可信度。
senses.why: In court, evidence that catches a witness in a contradiction sets a snare for that person credibility.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上，能抓住证人自相矛盾的证据，正是为他信誉设下的一张网。

senses.title: To be blamed or harmed in the old sense
senses.definition: in older use, to damage, hinder or bring harm to something
senses.definitionCN: 在较早的用法中，指损害、妨碍或给某事带来不利
senses.example: In his old speech he warned that such neglect would impeach the peace of the realm.
senses.exampleCN: 在那篇旧时演说里，他警告说这样的疏忽会损害王国的和平。
senses.why: The snare image can also mean being caught and held back, which explains the older sense of harm or hindrance.
senses.whyCN: 被网套住的画面也可以表示被困住、受阻，这就解释了「损害、妨碍」的旧义。

senses.title: To call a charge into question
senses.definition: to make an accusation against a thing or an action, often in a formal complaint
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或某项行为提出指责，常见于正式的申诉
senses.example: The traders impeached the new tax before the council.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们向议会指控这项新税。
senses.why: Anything that is formally brought up against another party keeps the shape of an accusation being presented.
senses.whyCN: 任何被正式摆到对方头上的事情，都保留着「当众提出指控」的形状。

senses.title: To question the value of a rule or practice
senses.definition: to suggest that an established rule, custom or principle is faulty or no longer sound
senses.definitionCN: 暗示某条既定的规则、习俗或原则有缺陷或已不再合理
senses.example: Critics impeach the idea that endless growth is always good.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者质疑「无休止的增长总是好事」这一观点。
senses.why: If a claim can be charged with error, so can an established rule, which is how the word reaches abstract principles.
senses.whyCN: 如果一种说法能被指控有错，既定规则也同样可以，这个词就是这样触及抽象原则的。

senses.title: To charge a head of state under a constitution
senses.definition: to accuse a president or a head of state of a constitutional offence in a special process
senses.definitionCN: 依照宪法规定的特别程序，指控总统或国家元首犯有违宪行为
senses.example: Under the constitution, only the house can impeach a president.
senses.exampleCN: 依照宪法，只有众议院有权弹劾总统。
senses.why: The modern political sense fixes the general legal charge onto the highest offices, giving a narrow and well known usage.
senses.whyCN: 现代政治义把一般性的法律指控固定到最高职位上，形成了狭窄而广为人知的用法。

intro.en: Impeach comes from Old French empechier, to hinder, from Late Latin impedicare, to entangle the feet, built on in- (into) and pes (foot).
intro.cn: impeach 来自古法语 empechier（阻碍），源自晚期拉丁语 impedicare（绊住脚），由 in-（进入）与 pes（脚）构成。

items.en: Pes means foot, and the Latin root pictures a foot caught in a loop or a snare.
items.cn: pes 意为「脚」，这个拉丁词根描绘的是一只脚被绳圈或罗网缠住。

items.en: Impedicare combines in- (into) with pedica (a fetter), meaning to entangle the feet and hold someone back.
items.cn: impedicare 把 in-（进入）与 pedica（脚镣）合在一起，意为缠住双脚、使人无法前进。

items.en: The verb becomes empechier in Old French, where it means to hinder or entrap.
items.cn: 这个动词在古法语中变为 empechier，意为阻碍或使陷入圈套。

items.en: Middle English impeachen carries the ideas of hindrance and of bringing a legal charge against someone.
items.cn: 中古英语 impeachen 同时带有「阻碍」与「对某人提出法律指控」两层意思。

items.en: The political meaning narrows towards a special charge against a public official, especially a president.
items.cn: 政治含义逐渐收窄，专指对公职人员、尤其是总统提出的特别指控。

items.en: Modern English keeps both branches: the political charge and the doubt cast on credibility or value.
items.cn: 现代英语同时保留两支：政治上的弹劾，以及对可信度或价值的质疑。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin foot-and-fetter root; the near-meaning group gathers words for accusing or doubting, from the formal to the general.
note.cn: 形近组收同样出自拉丁语「脚与脚镣」词根的词；近义组收表示指控或怀疑的词，从正式到一般。

entries.definition: To slow down or block progress; it shares the foot-and-fetter root with impeach.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「阻碍、拖延」，与 impeach 共享「脚与脚镣」的词根。

entries.definition: Something that holds a plan or a person back; the noun of impede.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「障碍、妨碍物」，是 impede 的名词形式。

entries.definition: The formal charge of misconduct against a public official; the noun of impeach.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「弹劾」，指对公职人员违规行为的正式指控，是 impeach 的名词。

entries.definition: To formally charge someone with a crime before a court; criminal law rather than politics.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「正式起诉、控告」，用于刑事法律程序而非政治程序。

entries.definition: To say that someone has done wrong; the plain everyday word for blame.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「指控、指责」，是最日常的责备用语。

entries.definition: To question whether something is true or right; broad and neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「质疑、挑战」，范围宽泛且中性。

normalIntro.en: Impeach grew from a picture of a foot caught in a snare, so it leans towards accusation and doubt.
normalIntro.cn: impeach 由「脚被网套住」的画面生长而来，因此语义偏向指控与质疑。

normal.en: The impedi- shape in this word is the same one seen in impede, and a snare holds someone in place.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 impedi- 形状也出现在 impede 中，罗网会把人在原地绊住。

normal.en: The usual frame is impeach someone for something, as in impeach the mayor for lying.
normal.cn: 常见框架是 impeach someone for something，如因说谎而弹劾市长。

normal.en: Impeachment is the charge itself, while removal from office is the separate final result.
normal.cn: impeachment 指指控本身，被免职则是另一回事的最终结果。

normal.en: Unimpeachable means beyond doubt and is the natural opposite of the doubt sense.
normal.cn: unimpeachable 意为「无可指责的」，正好是怀疑义项的反面配对。

normal.en: Compare with accuse: accuse is everyday, while impeach is formal and usually about officials or credibility.
normal.cn: 对比 accuse：accuse 属日常用语，impeach 正式，通常针对官员或可信度。

abstract.en: A rope loop closing around an ankle at the very moment the charge is read out.
abstract.cn: 宣读罪名的瞬间，一只绳圈在脚踝上收紧。

abstract.en: A giant finger pointing at a man on a podium while cameras flash.
abstract.cn: 闪光灯中，一根巨大的手指指向讲台上的那个人。

abstract.en: A sealed envelope marked with a formal charge slipping onto a judge desk.
abstract.cn: 一只封好并标注了正式指控的公文袋，滑到法官的桌上。

examples.en: Congress debated whether to impeach the president for abuse of power.
examples.cn: 国会辩论是否以滥用职权为由弹劾总统。

examples.en: A single error in the data can impeach the whole study.
examples.cn: 数据中的一处错误就可能让整项研究受到质疑。

examples.en: The widow gave an unimpeachable account of what happened that night.
examples.cn: 这位遗孀对那天夜里发生的事情作了不容置疑的陈述。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬批斥」——硬着脾气批一批、斥一斥，就是当面指控他；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pes（脚）→ pedica（脚镣）→ 晚期拉丁语 impedicare（绊住脚、使无法前进）→ 古法语 empechier（阻碍）→ 英语 impeach，从「设网绊住」演化为「控告、弹劾、质疑」。

sensesIntro.en: Impeach begins with the picture of a foot caught in a snare, which links hindrance with formal accusation and finally with doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: impeach 从「脚被网套住」的画面开始，把阻碍、正式指控，最终与质疑连成一条线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot caught in a rope loop while a charge is read aloud.
core.cn: 核心意象：宣读罪名的同时一只脚被绳圈套住。

branches.en: The political charge against high officials is the best known branch.
branches.cn: 针对高级官员的政治指控是最为人熟知的分支。

branches.en: The general legal accusation branch keeps the older courtroom use.
branches.cn: 一般的法律指控分支保留了较早的庭审用法。

branches.en: Doubt about credibility, witnesses and principles is the attack-on-trust branch.
branches.cn: 对可信度、证人和原则的怀疑，构成「冲击信任」的分支。

branches.en: Doubting a motive or a rule is a charge laid against hidden reasons.
branches.cn: 对动机或规则的怀疑，是针对隐藏理由提出的一桩指控。

branches.en: The old sense of harm and hindrance survives from the snare image.
branches.cn: 损害与妨碍的旧义存留在罗网意象之中。

intro.en: Impeach is built from the direction prefix in- and the Latin word for foot, which together give the image of caught feet.
intro.cn: impeach 由表示方向的前缀 in- 与拉丁语「脚」合构，合起来就是「脚被套住」的画面。

latinIntro.en: The Latin elements are in-, meaning into, and pes with its derivative pedica, a fetter or foot trap.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁成分是表示「进入」的 in-，以及 pes（脚）及其派生词 pedica（脚镣、捕脚圈套）。

items.example: The prefix shows the foot being put into the trap.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀显示脚被放进陷阱里。

items.example: Before p, in- becomes im-, as in impedicare.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，in- 变成 im-，如 impedicare。

items.example: The root ped- keeps the bodily picture of the word.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ped- 保留了这个词的身体画面。

items.example: Pes supplies the foot that gets caught.
items.exampleCN: pes 提供那只被套住的脚。

items.example: Pedica is the trap hidden in the verb.
items.exampleCN: pedica 就是藏在这个动词里的陷阱。

items.example: The suffix -ment forms impeachment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 impeachment。

items.example: Impeachment names the process of charging an official.
items.exampleCN: impeachment 指指控官员的程序。

items.example: The suffix -able forms impeachable.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -able 构成 impeachable。

items.example: The prefix un- makes unimpeachable, meaning beyond doubt.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unimpeachable，意为不容置疑。

items.meaningCN: 无可指责的；不容置疑的
items.example: Unimpeachable describes a reputation that cannot be attacked.
items.exampleCN: unimpeachable 形容无法被攻击的名声。

latinEntries.example: Pes is the body image inside the word.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pes 是藏在词里的身体意象。

latinEntries.example: Pedica gives the notion of being held back.
latinEntries.exampleCN: pedica 带来「被绊住」的概念。

latinEntries.example: Impedicare is the direct ancestor of impeach.
latinEntries.exampleCN: impedicare 是 impeach 的直接祖先。

definition_zh: 阻碍；妨碍；拖慢进度
definition_en: to slow down or block the progress of something, often without stopping it completely
core_image: 脚上缠着一副木枷，每走一步都被拖住
scene: 早高峰的地铁口有人被行李绊倒，人群堵在闸机前挪不动。Fallen luggage impeded the passengers leaving the station.
sceneCN: 这里 impede 是「阻碍」（第 01 个义项：拖慢事物前进的进度）；句意是散落的行李阻碍了乘客离开车站，道路并没有被封死，只是被人为拖慢了。

collocations.phrase: impede a person from doing something
