senses.title: To slow down progress
senses.definition: to make the progress of an activity or process slower and harder than it should be
senses.definitionCN: 使某项活动或进程的推进变得缓慢、困难
senses.example: Bad weather impeded the rescue work.
senses.exampleCN: 恶劣的天气阻碍了救援工作。
senses.why: The Latin root pes means foot, so the core image is a foot caught in a shackle; movement continues, only slowed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pes 意为「脚」，核心意象是一只脚被套住，能做的是步伐变慢，前进并没有停止。

senses.title: To obstruct movement
senses.definition: to block the way of traffic, people, or a flow so that they can barely move
senses.definitionCN: 挡住车流、人流的去路，使其几乎无法通行
senses.example: A fallen tree impeded traffic for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 一棵倒下的树让交通受阻了好几个小时。
senses.why: From the abstract slowing down grows a physical picture: an object placed on the road that holds the stream back.
senses.whyCN: 从抽象的拖慢延伸到具体的画面：路上横着一件东西，把原本流动的人流车流兜住。

senses.title: To hinder someone or something
senses.definition: to hinder a person, plan, or effort, usually by indirect means rather than open force
senses.definitionCN: 以间接手段妨碍某人、某项计划或努力
senses.example: Lack of funding impeded the project from the start.
senses.exampleCN: 资金不足从一开始就妨碍了这个项目。
senses.why: The prefix im- doubles the sense of being in the way, so the word often describes quiet, indirect obstruction.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 im- 强化了「横在途中」的感觉，所以这个词多指暗中、非正面的阻拦。

senses.title: A legal impediment
senses.definition: in law, a factor or circumstance that legally prevents an action or a marriage
senses.definitionCN: 法律上阻止某项行为或婚姻成立的因素或情形
senses.example: An existing marriage is a legal impediment to a second wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 已有婚姻关系是再次结婚的法律障碍。
senses.why: In legal Latin an impedimentum is a shackle; the figurative shackle became a formal obstacle.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语 impedimentum 本身就是「脚镣」，隐喻的镣铐在法律里就变成了正式障碍。

senses.title: To hamper speech
senses.definition: to interfere with speech or another physical function so that it is hard to perform
senses.definitionCN: 干扰说话或其他身体功能，使人难以完成
senses.example: A childhood injury impeded her speech.
senses.exampleCN: 童年的一次受伤影响了她的说话能力。
senses.why: The image extends from feet to other limbs and organs: anything that used to move freely is now held back.
senses.whyCN: 意象从脚扩展到其他肢体与器官：凡是本来能自由运作的，如今都被拖住了。

senses.title: Something that holds back growth
senses.definition: to limit the growth or improvement of a plant, body, or economy over time
senses.definitionCN: 长期限制植物、身体或经济的生长与改善
senses.example: Pests impeded the growth of the young trees.
senses.exampleCN: 虫害阻碍了小树的生长。
senses.why: When the slowing lasts for a long time, the meaning shifts from slow progress to stunted growth.
senses.whyCN: 当拖慢持续很久，词义就从「进度慢」转向「长不起来」。

intro.en: Impede comes from Latin impedire, to entangle the feet, from in- plus pes, the foot.
intro.cn: impede 来自拉丁语 impedire（缠住脚），由 in-（进入）与 pes（脚）构成。

items.en: Pes means the foot, and impedire means to entangle the feet.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pes 意为脚，impedire 意为缠住双脚。

items.en: Cicero and Livy use impedire for entangling troops and slowing an enemy.
items.cn: 西塞罗与李维用 impedire 表示缠住队伍、拖住敌人。

items.en: Impedimentum is a shackle, and its plural impedimenta means baggage.
items.cn: impedimentum 意为脚镣，其复数 impedimenta 指随军的行装。

items.en: English borrows the verb directly from Latin as impeden.
items.cn: 中古英语直接从拉丁语借入动词 impeden。

items.en: The modern spelling impede settles into use.
items.cn: 现代拼写 impede 在十六世纪固定下来。

items.en: Modern English broadens the verb to plans, trade, and research.
items.cn: 现代英语把动词扩展到计划、贸易与研究等领域。

note.en: Impede belongs to the foot family, with impediment and pedals, and is close to everyday words like hinder and obstruct.
note.cn: impede 属于「脚」词族，与 impediment、pedal 同源，同时与 hinder、obstruct 等日常词相邻。

entries.definition: something that delays or blocks progress
entries.definitionCN: 障碍物；阻碍

entries.definition: the baggage and supplies that slow an army
entries.definitionCN: 拖慢行军的行李与辎重

entries.definition: to make a process happen faster
entries.definitionCN: 加快；促进（字面义为「解开缠脚的东西」）

entries.definition: to make it harder for something to happen
entries.definitionCN: 妨碍；阻碍（与 impede 几乎同义，更常用）

entries.definition: to block a passage or prevent action outright
entries.definitionCN: 阻塞；阻挡（程度比 impede 更强）

entries.definition: to make movement or work awkward and slow
entries.definitionCN: 妨碍；束缚（侧重行动不便）

normalIntro.en: Impede is built from in- and pes, the Latin foot, so think of a foot caught in a shackle.
normalIntro.cn: impede 由 in- 与拉丁语 pes（脚）构成，记忆时想象一只被套住的脚。

normal.en: Remember pes: the same foot root gives pedal and pedestrian.
normal.cn: 记住 pes：同一个「脚」词根还构成 pedal 与 pedestrian。

normal.en: Impediment is the noun that goes with it, and legal texts speak of an impediment to marriage.
normal.cn: impediment 是它的名词，法律文书里说「结婚的障碍」。

normal.en: Expedite is its opposite, literally to free or untangle the feet.
normal.cn: expedite 是它的反义，字面上是「把脚解开、松开」。

normal.en: Impedimenta was the Roman word for heavy army baggage.
normal.cn: impedimenta 是罗马人行军时拖累速度的重行李。

normal.en: Compare hinder and obstruct: impede usually means slowing, not full stopping.
normal.cn: 对比 hinder 与 obstruct：impede 多指拖慢，而非彻底堵死。

abstract.en: Picture a runner whose shoelaces are tied together.
abstract.cn: 想象一个跑者的两根鞋带被系在一起。

abstract.en: Imagine a stream of traffic narrowing into one lane.
abstract.cn: 想象车流被挤到只剩一条车道。

abstract.en: Think of a plan weighed down by one missing permit.
abstract.cn: 想象一份计划只因为少了一张许可就被拖住。

examples.en: Heavy snow impeded the delivery of medicine to the village.
examples.cn: 大雪阻碍了药品运往村庄。

examples.en: A lack of clear rules often impedes trade between regions.
examples.cn: 规则不清常常妨碍地区之间的贸易。

examples.en: Thick fog impeded the search for the missing climber.
examples.cn: 浓雾妨碍了对失踪登山者的搜寻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬皮踹」——脚上套着硬皮的枷锁，想走也踹不开，路也就被拖住了；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ pes、ped-（脚）→ impedire（缠住脚）→ impedimentum（脚镣）→ 英语 impede，核心义「脚被绊住」。

sensesIntro.en: Impede starts from a foot in a shackle, then branches into traffic, plans, law, speech, and long term growth.
sensesIntro.cn: impede 从「脚被套住」出发，再扩展到交通、计划、法律、说话与长期生长等场景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foot caught in a wooden shackle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只脚被木枷套住。

branches.en: Slowing progress is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 拖慢进度是日常最常用的义项。

branches.en: Blocking movement is the traffic sense.
branches.cn: 阻塞通行是交通场景的义项。

branches.en: Hindering a person or plan is the abstract sense.
branches.cn: 妨碍人或计划是抽象层面的义项。

branches.en: Both slow things down, one in time and one in space.
branches.cn: 两者都是拖慢，一个在时间上，一个在空间上。

branches.en: Law, speech, and growth reuse the shackle as formal and long term blockage.
branches.cn: 法律、说话与生长把枷锁变成正式的、长期的阻塞。

intro.en: Impede is a Latin verb built on in- and the foot root ped-, with English impediment, expedite, and pedal in the same family.
intro.cn: impede 是以 in- 和「脚」词根 ped- 构成的拉丁动词，英语同族词有 impediment、expedite 与 pedal。

latinIntro.en: Latin pes is the foot, impedire is to entangle the feet, and impedimentum is a shackle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pes 是脚，impedire 是缠住脚，impedimentum 是脚镣。

items.example: The prefix in- gives the sense of getting in the way.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 带来「伸进路中」的感觉。

items.example: The root ped- appears in pedal and pedestrian.
items.exampleCN: 词根 ped- 出现在 pedal 与 pedestrian 中。

items.meaning: to entangle the feet, to hinder
items.example: Impedire is the direct Latin source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: impedire 是这个词的直接拉丁来源。

items.example: Impedimentum gives English impediment.
items.exampleCN: impedimentum 生出英语的 impediment。

items.meaning: result or means of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作结果或手段的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ment forms impediment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 impediment。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ance forms impedance.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ance 构成 impedance。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns the root into expedite, to free the feet.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把词根变成 expedite，意为「把脚解放出来」。

items.example: Expedite is the opposite of impede.
items.exampleCN: expedite 是 impede 的反义词。

items.example: Impede keeps the shackle image.
items.exampleCN: impede 保留着枷锁的意象。

items.example: Pedal shows the plain foot root.
items.exampleCN: pedal 展示了最朴素的「脚」词根。

latinEntries.meaning: to free the feet, to get ready

definition_zh: 驱使；促使；推动
definition_en: to push or drive someone to do something, often because of a strong inner force
core_image: 背后有一只手，把人往前一推
scene: 夜里她翻来覆去睡不着，心里有个声音催她立刻打电话道歉。A sudden sense of guilt impelled her to call her sister.
sceneCN: 这里 impel 是「驱使」（第 01 个义项：内心的力量推动人行动）；句意是突如其来的内疚感驱使她给姐姐打电话。是内在的推力，而非别人的命令。

collocations.zh: 感到不得不；觉得非……不可

derivatives.zh: 由同一拉丁词根 pellere 构成，义为「冲动；推动力」
由 impel 加名词后缀 -sion 构成，义为「推动；冲动的驱使」
由 impulse 加 -ive 构成，义为「冲动的；凭一时冲动行事的」
前缀换成 com-（一起、强力），义为「强迫」，力度比 impel 更硬

senses.title: To be driven by a feeling
senses.definition: to push someone to act because of a strong emotion, belief, or urge inside them
senses.definitionCN: 因强烈的情绪、信念或内心冲动而推动某人行动
senses.example: Curiosity impelled her to open the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心驱使她打开了那封信。
senses.why: The Latin root pellere means to strike or drive, so the core image is a hand pushing from behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 pellere 意为「击打、推动」，核心意象是背后有一只手在推。

senses.title: To force out of necessity
senses.definition: to make an action unavoidable, so that the person feels there is little choice
senses.definitionCN: 使某项行动不可避免，当事人几乎别无选择
senses.example: Poverty impelled the family to move to the city.
senses.exampleCN: 贫穷迫使这家人搬到了城里。
senses.why: When the pushing hand is circumstance rather than feeling, the verb approaches the sense of being forced.
senses.whyCN: 当推手从情绪换成处境时，词义就逼近「被迫」。

senses.title: To set something in motion
senses.definition: to give an object or process the push that starts it moving
senses.definitionCN: 给物体或进程一股推力，让它开始运转
senses.example: The wind impelled the small boat toward the shore.
senses.exampleCN: 风把小船推向岸边。
senses.why: Before it describes people, the Latin verb drives physical objects, so the mechanical push stays in the word.
senses.whyCN: 在用来写人之前，这个拉丁动词本是推动实物，所以「机械推力」的意义仍留在词里。

senses.title: A sense of moral duty
senses.definition: to feel that duty or conscience requires an action, expressed with the passive verb
senses.definitionCN: 觉得责任或良心要求自己做某事，常用被动形式
senses.example: She felt impelled to report what she had seen.
senses.exampleCN: 她觉得非把看到的事报告出来不可。
senses.why: The outer push becomes an inner voice, and English marks this with the passive form.
senses.whyCN: 外在的推手变成了内心的声音，英语习惯用被动形式表达这种压力。

senses.title: To drive forward energetically
senses.definition: to give energy or momentum that carries a movement forward at speed
senses.definitionCN: 给出能量或势头，让运动快速向前
senses.example: The lively crowd impelled the dancers to move faster.
senses.exampleCN: 活跃的观众让舞者跳得更起劲了。
senses.why: Speed belongs to the strike of the original verb, and an impelling force carries motion along.
senses.whyCN: 「速度」来自原动词的击打感，推力一起，运动也就一路带下去。

intro.en: Impel comes from Latin impellere, to push against or drive on, from in- plus pellere, to drive.
intro.cn: impel 来自拉丁语 impellere（推动、驱使），由 in-（向内）与 pellere（推动）构成。

items.en: Pellere means to strike, drive, or drive away.
items.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 意为击打、推动或赶走。

items.en: Impellere is to push into motion or drive a person to act.
items.cn: impellere 意为推入运动之中，或驱使一个人行动。

items.en: It is common in classical prose for emotions that drive people to act.
items.cn: 在古典散文中，它常用于情绪驱使人行动。

items.en: English borrows impellen from Latin rather than through French.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁语直接借入 impellen，而不是经由法语。

items.en: The modern spelling impel and the passive sense of being forced settle in.
items.cn: 现代拼写 impel 与「被迫」的被动用法固定下来。

note.en: Impel shares the Latin root pellere with compel, expel, and repel, and is close to urge and drive.
note.cn: impel 与 compel、expel、repel 共享拉丁词根 pellere，并与 urge、drive 等词相邻。

entries.definition: to force someone by authority or circumstance
entries.definitionCN: 强迫（力度比 impel 更硬，几乎没有选择）

entries.definition: to push someone or something out
entries.definitionCN: 驱逐；排出（字面义为「往外推」）

entries.definition: to drive something back or away
entries.definitionCN: 击退；排斥

entries.definition: to strongly encourage someone to act
entries.definitionCN: 敦促；力劝（更口语，力度较轻）

entries.definition: to force or lead someone to do something
entries.definitionCN: 驱使；逼迫（最宽泛的说法）

entries.definition: to persuade or cause someone to do something
entries.definitionCN: 诱导；引起（偏说服，而非强推）

normalIntro.en: Impel is in- plus pellere, to drive, so the same root appears in compel, expel, and repel.
normalIntro.cn: impel 是 in- 加 pellere（推动），同一个词根也构成 compel、expel 与 repel。

normal.en: Compare compel: compel makes you obey, impel makes you want to act.
normal.cn: 对比 compel：compel 是逼你服从，impel 是让你想去做。

normal.en: Note the double l in impelled and impelling, like compelled.
normal.cn: 注意 impelled 与 impelling 里的双写 l，与 compelled 同理。

normal.en: The common frame is be impelled to do something.
normal.cn: 常见结构是 be impelled to do something。

normal.en: Impulse is the noun of the same push, as in a sudden impulse.
normal.cn: impulse 是同源名词，如「突然的冲动」。

normal.en: Repel, expel, and propel all keep the idea of driving.
normal.cn: repel、expel、propel 都保留着「推动」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on your back, gently but firmly pushing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手按在你背上，不重却很坚定地推着。

abstract.en: Imagine a gust of wind filling one sail.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵风鼓满一张帆。

abstract.en: Think of guilt as a small voice saying go, go now.
abstract.cn: 把愧疚想成一个小声催促「去，现在就去」的声音。

examples.en: A sense of duty impelled him to work late every night.
examples.cn: 责任感驱使他每晚都加班到很晚。

examples.en: She was impelled by curiosity to read the old diary.
examples.cn: 好奇心驱使她去读那本旧日记。

examples.en: The noise outside impelled everyone to look up at once.
examples.cn: 外面的噪音让所有人都立刻抬起头来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬偏」——有人让你硬往一边偏，也就是把你推着走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ pellere（推、击）→ impellere（推入、驱使）→ 英语 impel，核心义「在人背后推一把」。

sensesIntro.en: Impel begins with a physical push, then moves to inner feelings, necessity, duty, and energetic momentum.
sensesIntro.cn: impel 从身体的推力出发，再扩展到内心情绪、现实逼迫、道义责任与冲劲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing hard against a back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手用力推着后背。

branches.en: The feeling sense is the most common one today.
branches.cn: 被情绪驱使是今天最常用的义项。

branches.en: Circumstances can push as firmly as feelings do.
branches.cn: 现实的处境和情绪一样能推人。

branches.en: The physical push survives in descriptions of objects.
branches.cn: 对实物的推动仍保留物理意义的用法。

branches.en: Both involve an inner force that leaves no rest.
branches.cn: 两者都是内心有股力量，让人不得安宁。

branches.en: Both carry momentum, one of an object and one of an action.
branches.cn: 两者都有势头，一个是物体，一个是行动。

intro.en: Impel is a Latin root verb: the prefix tells you the direction and pellere supplies the push.
intro.cn: impel 是典型的拉丁词根动词：前缀决定方向，pellere 提供推力。

latinIntro.en: Latin pellere means to drive or strike, so every verb with this root contains the idea of a push.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pellere 意为推动、击打，凡带这个词根的动词都含有推的意思。

items.example: The prefix in- points the push forward.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把推力指向前方。

items.example: Pellere is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: pellere 是整个词族的根。

items.example: Impellere is the direct source of impel.
items.exampleCN: impellere 是 impel 的直接来源。

items.example: The prefix com- turns the root into compel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 com- 把词根变成 compel。

items.example: The prefix ex- turns the root into expel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ex- 把词根变成 expel。

items.example: The prefix re- turns the root into repel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 把词根变成 repel。

items.example: The prefix pro- turns the root into propel.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pro- 把词根变成 propel。

items.meaning: state or result of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示动作状态或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -sion forms impulsion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -sion 构成 impulsion。

items.example: Impulse shares the same drive.
items.exampleCN: impulse 共享同一种推力。

items.example: Impel keeps the inward push.
items.exampleCN: impel 保留了向内推的方向。

definition_zh: 紧急必要的；极重要的；命令的；祈使语气；必要的事
definition_en: extremely important and urgent, or a command, or the verb form used for giving orders
core_image: 指挥官抬手指向路口，下令立刻出发
scene: 洪水已经漫过堤岸，镇长站上桌子，要先救老人和孩子。It is imperative that the villagers leave before nightfall.
sceneCN: 这里 imperative 是「紧急必要的」（第 01 个义项：事情紧急，非做不可）；句意是村民必须在天黑前撤离。语气像一道命令，不容商量。

pos.zh: 紧急必要的；极重要的；命令的
必要的事；祈使语气；命令

collocations.phrase: it is imperative to do something

derivatives.zh: 由 imperative 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「以命令的口吻」
由 imperative 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧迫性」
同根拉丁词，义为「统帅」，罗马皇帝称号的来源
同根形容词，义为「专横的；盛气凌人的」

senses.title: Extremely urgent and necessary
senses.definition: so important that action cannot be delayed and must be taken at once
senses.definitionCN: 重要到不能拖延、必须马上采取行动
senses.example: It is imperative to act before the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 必须在截止日期前行动起来。
senses.why: The Latin root imperare means to command, and a command leaves no room for delay.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 imperare 意为命令，命令不给拖延留余地，所以成了「必须立刻做」。

senses.title: Very important
senses.definition: of the highest importance, spoken of a matter, duty, or need
senses.definitionCN: 具有最高的重要性，用于形容事务、职责或需要
senses.example: Training is an imperative need for the new staff.
senses.exampleCN: 对新员工来说，培训是迫切需要。
senses.why: The word can point at the weight of a matter rather than its speed.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以指向事情的分量，而不只是速度，于是有了「极重要」。

senses.title: Commanding, like an order
senses.definition: having the tone or authority of a command
senses.definitionCN: 带有命令的口吻或权威
senses.example: Her imperative voice silenced the room.
senses.exampleCN: 她那命令式的嗓音让全场安静下来。
senses.why: The oldest sense of the Latin source is the giving of orders, and that tone survives in English.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁来源最古老的意思是下达命令，这种口吻在英语里保留了下来。

senses.title: The imperative mood
senses.definition: in grammar, the verb form used for orders, requests, and instructions
senses.definitionCN: 语法上用于命令、请求与指示的动词形式
senses.example: In the sentence sit down, the verb is in the imperative.
senses.exampleCN: 在 sit down 这个句子里，动词用的是祈使语气。
senses.why: Grammar names the order-giving verb form after the very idea of commanding.
senses.whyCN: 语法用「命令」这个概念来命名下命令的动词形式。

senses.title: Something that must be done
senses.definition: a principle, duty, or task that is treated as absolutely necessary
senses.definitionCN: 被视为绝对必要的原则、职责或任务
senses.example: Honesty became a moral imperative for the company.
senses.exampleCN: 诚信成了这家公司道义上的必行之事。
senses.why: When the adjective is used as a noun, the urgent order becomes a thing you must carry out.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转为名词后，那道紧急命令就变成了一件你必须完成的事。

senses.title: A philosophical duty
senses.definition: in ethics, a rule that binds everyone, most famously in Kants categorical imperative
senses.definitionCN: 伦理上对所有人都有约束力的准则，最著名的是康德的「绝对命令」
senses.example: The categorical imperative asks us to act on universal principles.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对命令要求人们依据普遍原则行动。
senses.why: Philosophy turns the commanding force into a principle that binds every rational person.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把这种命令般的力量变成一条约束每个理性人的准则。

intro.en: Imperative comes from Latin imperare, to command, from in- plus parare, to prepare or order.
intro.cn: imperative 来自拉丁语 imperare（命令），由 in-（向内）与 parare（准备、安排）构成。

items.en: Parare means to prepare or arrange, and imperare builds on it with the idea of ordering.
items.cn: 拉丁语 parare 意为准备、安排，imperare 在此之上发展出「下令」的意思。

items.en: Imperare is the standard verb of the Roman state for issuing orders.
items.cn: 在罗马国家事务中，imperare 是下达命令的常用动词。

items.en: Imperativus means apt to command and is borrowed into grammar for the moods of orders.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 imperativus 意为「与命令有关的」，被语法学借用去指命令式。

items.en: The form passes into Old French as imperatif.
items.cn: 该词形传入古法语写作 imperatif。

items.en: English borrows it as both adjective and noun.
items.cn: 英语借入后同时用作形容词和名词。

items.en: Modern use extends from grammar to ethics and everyday urgency.
items.cn: 现代用法从语法扩展到伦理与日常的紧迫表达。

note.en: Imperative shares the root imperare with emperor and imperious, and sits near urgent and compulsory.
note.cn: imperative 与 emperor、imperious 共享词根 imperare，语义上与 urgent、compulsory 相邻。

entries.definition: a Roman commander, later the title of emperor
entries.definitionCN: 罗马统帅，后来成为皇帝的称号

entries.definition: bossy and expecting obedience
entries.definitionCN: 专横的；盛气凌人的（多带贬义）

entries.definition: the ruler of an empire
entries.definitionCN: 皇帝；君主

entries.definition: needing action right away
entries.definitionCN: 紧急的（强调时间紧）

entries.definition: absolutely necessary to exist or work
entries.definitionCN: 必不可少的（强调缺不得）

entries.definition: required by law or rule
entries.definitionCN: 强制的；义务的（强调制度规定）

normalIntro.en: Imperative comes from imperare, to command, so think of a father figure with absolute authority.
normalIntro.cn: imperative 来自 imperare（命令），联想一位拥有绝对权威的统帅。

normal.en: The standard pattern is it is imperative that plus a subject and the base verb.
normal.cn: 标准句型是「it is imperative that」加主语和动词原形。

normal.en: Emperor and imperator share the root, and so does the adjective imperious.
normal.cn: emperor 与 imperator 共享词根，形容词 imperious 也是同族。

normal.en: In grammar the imperative is the form used for orders such as stop and look.
normal.cn: 语法上，祈使式用于 stop、look 这类命令。

normal.en: Kant wrote of the categorical imperative, a rule that binds everyone.
normal.cn: 康德写过「绝对命令」，即对所有人都有效的准则。

normal.en: Compare urgent and essential: imperative combines both time pressure and importance.
normal.cn: 对比 urgent 与 essential：imperative 兼有时间紧与很重要两层。

abstract.en: Picture a general lifting one finger before a silent army.
abstract.cn: 想象一位将军在鸦雀无声的军队前抬起一根手指。

abstract.en: Imagine a red light that cannot be ignored.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏无法忽视的红灯。

abstract.en: Think of a bell that rings once and everyone stands up.
abstract.cn: 想象一口钟只响一声，所有人都站起来。

examples.en: It is imperative that we reduce waste in the factory.
examples.cn: 我们必须减少工厂里的浪费。

examples.en: For the club, safety is an imperative rather than a choice.
examples.cn: 对这个俱乐部来说，安全是必须做到的事，而不是可选项。

examples.en: The teacher used the imperative to tell the pupils to line up.
examples.cn: 老师用祈使语气叫学生们排队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬怕若停」——硬着头皮怕也得停不下来，被命令着不停往前；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内）+ parare（准备、安排）→ imperare（命令）+ -ivus（形容词词尾）→ 英语 imperative，核心义「下命令、不容迟延」。

sensesIntro.en: Imperative begins as the word for giving orders, then covers urgency, importance, grammar, and moral duty.
sensesIntro.cn: imperative 最初指下达命令，随后扩展到紧迫、重要、语法术语与道德责任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a commander giving an order that cannot be refused.
core.cn: 核心意象：指挥官下达无可推辞的命令。

branches.en: Something urgent is something ordered by time.
branches.cn: 紧急的事就像被时间下了命令。

branches.en: Importance is the weight behind the order.
branches.cn: 重要性就是命令背后的分量。

branches.en: The commanding tone is the closest to the Latin sense.
branches.cn: 命令口吻是最接近拉丁原义的义项。

branches.en: Grammar borrows the word for the verb form of orders.
branches.cn: 语法借这个词来指下命令的动词形式。

branches.en: As a noun it becomes a thing or principle that must be carried out.
branches.cn: 作名词时，它变成必须执行的事或准则。

intro.en: Imperative is a Latin root word: imperare supplies the command, and -ive makes the adjective.
intro.cn: imperative 是拉丁词根词：imperare 提供「命令」之义，-ive 使其成为形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin imperare means to command, and imperativus means apt to command.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 imperare 意为命令，imperativus 意为「与命令有关的」。

items.example: The prefix in- sets up the act of arranging.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 引出「安排、布置」的动作。

items.example: Parare also gives English prepare.
items.exampleCN: parare 也是英语 prepare 的来源。

items.example: Imperare is the direct source of imperative.
items.exampleCN: imperare 是 imperative 的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ive forms imperative from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 由拉丁词干构成 imperative。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms imperatively.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 imperatively。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ness forms imperativeness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 imperativeness。

items.example: The suffix -ator forms imperator, a commander.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ator 构成 imperator，即统帅。

items.example: Imperator shows the ruling sense of the root.
items.exampleCN: imperator 展示了词根里「统治」的一面。

items.example: Emperor grew from the same Latin root.
items.exampleCN: emperor 也由同一个拉丁词根发展而来。

items.example: Imperative carries the command into daily English.
items.exampleCN: imperative 把「命令」带进了日常英语。

definition_zh: 难以察觉的；感觉不到的；极其细微的
definition_en: too slight or gradual to be noticed by the senses or by the mind
core_image: 窗帘被风吹动，几乎看不出在动
scene: 老人盯着墙角，发现墙纸正一点点泛黄。The old man stared at the corner and saw the wallpaper turning yellow by an imperceptible degree.
sceneCN: 这里 imperceptible 是「难以察觉的」（第 1 个义项：细微到感觉不到）；句意：老人盯着墙角，发现墙纸正一点一点地泛黄，几乎察觉不到。

pos.zh: 难以察觉的；感觉不到的；极细微的

derivatives.zh: 难以察觉地；逐渐地
难以察觉性；细微
由 in- 的反义前缀脱落而来，意为「可察觉的」
「感知」动词，与 perceptible 同出一源

senses.title: Too slight to be noticed
senses.definition: so small, gradual, or slight that it cannot be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 小、缓或轻微到无法被人注意到
senses.example: There was an imperceptible change in her tone.
senses.exampleCN: 她的语气有了一丝几乎察觉不到的变化。
senses.why: The prefix in- means not and the root cap- means to take or grasp, so something imperceptible cannot be grasped by the senses.
senses.whyCN: 否定前缀 in- 加上词根 cap-（拿、抓），合起来就是「抓不住、感觉不到」；细微的变化溜过感官，所以自然长出了这个义项。

senses.title: Beyond the reach of the senses
senses.definition: not able to be heard, seen, felt, or otherwise detected by the senses
senses.definitionCN: 无法被听见、看见、感觉到或以其他方式察觉的
senses.example: The sound was almost imperceptible to human ears.
senses.exampleCN: 这个声音人耳几乎听不到。
senses.why: The root ties the word to perception itself, so it can describe anything outside the range of sight, hearing, or touch.
senses.whyCN: 词根与「感知」直接相连，所以凡超出视觉、听觉、触觉范围的刺激，都可以用这个词说「感觉不到」。

senses.title: So gradual as to be overlooked
senses.definition: happening so slowly and continuously that people do not see it happening
senses.definitionCN: 发生得太缓慢、太连续，以至于人们看不到它在发生
senses.example: The decline in the local dialect was imperceptible year by year.
senses.exampleCN: 当地方言的衰落逐年发生，慢得难以察觉。
senses.why: Once the image is a change too fine to catch, it can describe slow change that only shows up in long hindsight.
senses.whyCN: 意象是「细到抓不住的变动」，于是也能指那种必须靠长时间回顾才看出的缓慢变化，这是从「细」走向「渐变」的延伸。

senses.title: The philosophical unknowable
senses.definition: in philosophy, something that by nature cannot be perceived by the senses
senses.definitionCN: 在哲学中，指本质上无法被感官感知的事物
senses.example: The lecture discussed objects imperceptible to the human senses.
senses.exampleCN: 讲座讨论了人类感官无法感知的物体。
senses.why: From the everyday sense, philosophy borrows the word for things placed beyond any possible perception.
senses.whyCN: 哲学从日常义借走这个词，用来指被排除在一切可能感知之外的对象，是从「暂未察觉」推到「原则上不可察觉」。

intro.en: Imperceptible joins the Latin prefix in-, meaning not, to perceptible, from percipio, to take in or perceive.
intro.cn: imperceptible 由拉丁语否定前缀 in-（不）加 perceptible（可感知的）构成，后者源自 percipio（接收、感知）。

items.en: Percipio joins per-, through, and capio, to take or grasp.
items.cn: percipio 由 per-（穿过）与 capio（拿、抓）组成。

items.en: Perceptibilis means able to be perceived.
items.cn: perceptibilis 意为可被感知的。

items.en: Imperceptibilis adds in- to mean not able to be perceived.
items.cn: imperceptibilis 加上 in-，意为不可感知的。

items.en: The learned word passes into Scholastic and medieval scientific writing.
items.cn: 这个学术词进入经院哲学与中世纪科学写作。

items.en: English learns the word from learnt Latin, and it settles as an adjective for tiny changes.
items.cn: 英语经由书面拉丁语引入该词，逐渐定形为形容细微变化的形容词。

items.en: The adverb imperceptibly and the noun imperceptibility join it in the scientific vocabulary.
items.cn: 现代英语里，副词 imperceptibly 与名词 imperceptibility 一同进入科学词汇。

note.en: Imperceptible sits in the Latin cap- family of grasping and perceiving, and points at things under the threshold of notice.
note.cn: imperceptible 属于拉丁语 cap-（抓、取）词族，指落在注意门槛之下的细微事物。

entries.definition: so slightly that it cannot be noticed
entries.definitionCN: 难以察觉地

entries.definition: the quality of being hard to notice
entries.definitionCN: 难以察觉的性质

entries.definition: able to be noticed or felt
entries.definitionCN: 可感知的；同源而意义相反

entries.definition: lacking the ability to notice or understand things quickly
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏洞察力的；与目标词拼写相近，但词义不同

entries.definition: impossible to find out or discover
entries.definitionCN: 无法探测到的；更强调仪器检测

entries.definition: not able to be seen
entries.definitionCN: 看不见的；只在视觉范围内使用

entries.definition: very weak or slight
entries.definitionCN: 微弱的；勉强能察觉的

entries.definition: not obvious and hard to notice or describe
entries.definitionCN: 微妙的；不易注意的

normalIntro.en: Imperceptible is perceptible wearing a Latin not: if you cannot take it in, you cannot perceive it.
normalIntro.cn: imperceptible 就是给可感知的 perceptible 加上拉丁语否定前缀：接收不到，就感知不到。

normal.en: Take perceptible, the adjective of perceive, and add the not-prefix in-.
normal.cn: 取感知动词 perceive 的形容词形式 perceptible，再加否定前缀 in-。

normal.en: The adverb imperceptibly pairs with verbs of change: it shifted imperceptibly.
normal.cn: 副词 imperceptibly 常搭配变化类动词，如「它不知不觉地变了」。

normal.en: Common partners are change, difference, and movement, because they describe what the eye barely catches.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是变化、差别与动作，因为它们正描述眼睛几乎抓不住的东西。

normal.en: Use imperceptible to, as in imperceptible to the touch or to the ear.
normal.cn: 常用 imperceptible to 结构，如「摸不出」「听不见」。

normal.en: Compare inaudible and invisible: those name one missing sense, while imperceptible covers them all.
normal.cn: 对比 inaudible 与 invisible：那两个只限一种感官，imperceptible 则涵盖全部感官。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain moving a hair in a draft that no one feels.
abstract.cn: 想象一阵没人能感觉到的风，把窗帘吹动了一丝。

abstract.en: Think of a sound pitched just beyond the edge of hearing.
abstract.cn: 想象一个刚好超出听觉范围的声音。

abstract.en: Imagine watching a glacier, where nothing seems to move until you look back a year.
abstract.cn: 想象盯着冰川看，什么都在动，直到一年后回头才发现它走了很远。

examples.en: The change in the recipe was so small it was almost imperceptible.
examples.cn: 配方的改动很小，几乎察觉不到。

examples.en: Colours in the painting have faded in a way that is imperceptible to the naked eye.
examples.cn: 画作的色彩以肉眼无法察觉的方式褪去。

examples.en: Her breathing was imperceptible under the thick blanket.
examples.cn: 厚厚的毯子下，她的呼吸几乎听不出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬迫塞不得」——用力逼着去塞、去感觉，却怎么也塞不进感觉里；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ perceptibilis（可被感知的，源自 percipere「接收、感知」← per-「穿过」+ capere「抓取」）→ 英语 imperceptible，核心义「抓不住、感觉不到」。

sensesIntro.en: Imperceptible starts with a change too small to notice, widens to anything outside the senses, then stretches to slow hidden change and to the philosophical unknowable.
sensesIntro.cn: imperceptible 先指小到察觉不到的变化，再扩展到一切感官之外的刺激，然后延伸到缓慢难见的渐变与哲学上的不可感知。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain stirring in a draft no one can feel.
core.cn: 核心意象：一阵没人感觉到的风，让窗帘微微动了动。

branches.en: The everyday sense is a change so slight it slips past attention.
branches.cn: 日常义项是细微到溜过注意力的变化。

branches.en: The sensory sense names anything outside sight, hearing, or touch.
branches.cn: 感官义项指一切超出视觉、听觉、触觉范围的东西。

branches.en: Slow continuous change borrows the same threshold image.
branches.cn: 缓慢连续的变化借用了同一个「低于门槛」的意象。

branches.en: Philosophy pushes the word past any possible perception.
branches.cn: 哲学把这个词推到一切可能感知之外。

branches.en: Both the sensory and the philosophical sense rest on the idea of a perception that never happens.
branches.cn: 感官义与哲学义都建立在同一点上：感知永远不会发生。

intro.en: Imperceptible is built from the Latin pieces in-, per-, and cap-, with English perceptible, perceive, and perception as its family.
intro.cn: imperceptible 由拉丁语成分 in-、per-、cap- 构成，英语中的 perceptible、perceive、perception 是它的同族词。

latinIntro.en: The key Latin verb is percipere, from per, through, and capere, to take, giving the image of taking something in.
latinIntro.cn: 关键的拉丁语动词是 percipere，由 per（穿过）与 capere（拿取）构成，意象是「把东西接进来」。

items.example: In- turns perceptible into its opposite.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把 perceptible 变成它的反义词。

items.example: Per- shows an act passing all the way through.
items.exampleCN: per- 表示动作完全穿透。

items.example: The cap- root also appears in capture and capable.
items.exampleCN: cap- 词根也出现在 capture 与 capable 中。

items.example: Percipere is the source verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: percipere 是这一词族的源头动词。

items.example: Perceptibilis is the stem of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: perceptibilis 是英语形容词的词干。

items.example: The Latin word joins in- to perceptibilis.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词把 in- 加到了 perceptibilis 上。

items.example: The -ible suffix marks a passive ability.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 表示被动能力。

items.example: Perceptible is the positive partner of the target word.
items.exampleCN: perceptible 是目标词的反义搭档。

items.meaning: in a way that cannot be noticed
items.example: Imperceptibly describes how slow change happens.
items.exampleCN: imperceptibly 描述缓慢变化发生的方式。

items.meaningCN: 表性质或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The -ity suffix forms the abstract noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ity 构成抽象名词。

definition_zh: 使陷于危险；危及；危害
definition_en: to put someone or something at risk of harm or loss
core_image: 一个人把别人推向悬崖边缘
scene: 河岸被冲垮，洪水正逼近村子。Rising floodwater imperils the houses along the bank.
sceneCN: 这里 imperil 是「使陷于危险」（第 1 个义项：把某人或某物置于险境）；句意：上涨的洪水正威胁着岸边的房屋。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ment 构成，义为「危险；危及」
基础名词，义为「危险；险境」，imperil 即由它加前缀构成
由 peril 加 -ous 构成，义为「危险的；险恶的」

senses.title: To put at risk of harm
senses.definition: to put a person, place, or thing in danger of being harmed
senses.definitionCN: 把人、地方或事物置于受到伤害的危险中
senses.example: Careless logging imperils the village water supply.
senses.exampleCN: 滥伐林木危及村庄的供水。
senses.why: The prefix in- makes something enter a state, and peril means danger, so to imperil is literally to lead someone into danger.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 表示「进入某种状态」，peril 是危险，合起来就是把某人领进危险之中，所以核心义就是「置于险境」。

senses.title: To threaten something valued
senses.definition: to threaten something important such as peace, health, freedom, or a species
senses.definitionCN: 威胁和平、健康、自由或物种等重要事物
senses.example: The new law imperils press freedom.
senses.exampleCN: 这项新法律威胁新闻自由。
senses.why: When the object is something valuable and abstract, the verb reads as to threaten, which is the most common modern use.
senses.whyCN: 当宾语是和平、自由这类珍贵的抽象事物时，这个动词自然读作「威胁」，这也是今天最常见的用法。

senses.title: To ruin by one wrong move
senses.definition: to run the risk of destroying a chance, plan, or relationship by a careless action
senses.definitionCN: 因轻率的举动而使机会、计划或关系面临被毁掉的风险
senses.example: One careless remark imperilled the whole agreement.
senses.exampleCN: 一句不慎的话差点毁了整份协议。
senses.why: Because danger is entered by a concrete step, the verb can frame a single reckless act as the step that endangers a whole outcome.
senses.whyCN: 既然险境是「一步一步走进去」的，这个动词就能把某个鲁莽举动说成让整个结果陷入危险的那一步。

intro.en: Imperil is a learned English formation: the Latin prefix in-, meaning into, plus the noun peril, with the final consonant doubled.
intro.cn: imperil 是英语后期仿古构造：拉丁语前缀 in-（进入）加名词 peril（危险），词尾 l 重复。

items.en: Periculum means a trial, experiment, or danger.
items.cn: periculum 意为试验、尝试，进而指危险。

items.en: The suffix -culum is a small-forming instrumental suffix, and the making of periculum is debated.
items.cn: 后缀 -culum 是指小的工具类后缀，但它如何构成 periculum 学界尚有争论。

items.en: Peril, from Latin perīculum, names danger in French and later in English.
items.cn: peril 源自拉丁语 perīculum，先在法语、后在英语中指危险。

items.en: The noun peril is established in English by the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 peril 在十四世纪已进入英语并确立。

items.en: English coins the verb imperil by adding in- to peril, doubling the l.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪给 peril 加上 in- 造出动词 imperil，并重复了 l。

items.en: The spelling doubles the l in British English but keeps a single l in American usage.
items.cn: 现代英语中英式拼写重复 l，美式拼写只用一个 l。

note.en: Imperil belongs to the Latin periculum family of danger words, and sits close to the everyday verbs of threatening.
note.cn: imperil 属于拉丁语 periculum（危险）词族，与日常表示「威胁」的动词义近。

entries.definition: serious and immediate danger
entries.definitionCN: 基础名词，义为「严重的危险」

entries.definition: full of danger
entries.definitionCN: 由 peril 派生，义为「危险的」

entries.definition: the act of putting something in danger
entries.definitionCN: 由动词派生，义为「使陷险境」

entries.definition: to put someone or something in danger
entries.definitionCN: 使处于危险中；最常用的近义动词

entries.definition: to put something at risk of being harmed or lost
entries.definitionCN: 使面临损失或损害的风险；偏书面

entries.definition: to be likely to harm or destroy
entries.definitionCN: 威胁；有危害或毁坏的可能

normalIntro.en: Imperil is peril with a Latin in- in front: the act of leading something into danger.
normalIntro.cn: imperil 就是在 peril（危险）前面加上拉丁语前缀 in-：把某物带进危险。

normal.en: Take the noun peril and add the prefix in-, which marks entering a state.
normal.cn: 取名词 peril，加上表示「进入某状态」的前缀 in-。

normal.en: The spelling doubles the l: imperilled, imperilling, but American imperiled.
normal.cn: 拼写要重复 l：imperilled、imperilling，美式则写 imperiled。

normal.en: Typical objects are abstract and precious: health, peace, freedom, a species.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是抽象而珍贵的东西：健康、和平、自由、物种。

normal.en: Adverbs like seriously or gravely often sit before it.
normal.cn: seriously、gravely 这类副词常放在它前面。

normal.en: Compare endanger: imperil is more formal and more literary.
normal.cn: 对比 endanger：imperil 更正式、更有文学色彩。

abstract.en: Picture a hand shoving a person one step closer to the cliff edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把人往悬崖边推了一步。

abstract.en: Think of a leak quietly threatening a whole ship below the waterline.
abstract.cn: 想象船底一处细小的渗漏，正悄悄危及整条船。

abstract.en: Imagine a single careless word shaking a stack of balanced plates.
abstract.cn: 想象一句无心的话晃动了叠得整整齐齐的盘子。

examples.en: Climate change imperils coastal cities around the world.
examples.cn: 气候变化危及世界各地的沿海城市。

examples.en: The scandal imperilled his chances of re-election.
examples.cn: 这起丑闻危及他连任的机会。

examples.en: Poachers imperil the remaining population of rhinos.
examples.cn: 偷猎者危及剩余的犀牛种群。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「引破罗」——把船引到破了的罗盘边上，就是在把人往险处带；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ periculum（危险；试验）→ 古法语 peril（危险）→ 英语 peril → 十六世纪加 in- 构成动词 imperil，核心义「带进危险」。

sensesIntro.en: Imperil begins with putting a concrete person or thing in danger, then applies to precious abstractions, and finally frames a single careless act as what endangers an outcome.
sensesIntro.cn: imperil 先从把具体的人或物置于险境出发，再用于珍贵的抽象事物，最后把单个鲁莽举动说成危及整个结果的那一步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing someone toward the edge of a cliff.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把人推向悬崖边缘。

branches.en: The base sense is leading a person, place, or thing into danger.
branches.cn: 基础义项是把人、地方或事物领进危险。

branches.en: With an abstract object, the verb reads as threatening something valuable.
branches.cn: 宾语是抽象事物时，这个动词读作对珍贵之物的威胁。

branches.en: One reckless step can be framed as the act that endangers an outcome.
branches.cn: 一个鲁莽举动可以被说成危及整个结果的那一步。

branches.en: Whether the object is a house or public health, the pattern is the same: harm is made likely.
branches.cn: 无论宾语是房屋还是公众健康，模式都一样：让伤害变得可能。

branches.en: A careless word threatens a whole agreement, joining threat with a single step.
branches.cn: 一句不慎的话威胁整份协议，把威胁与单独一步连在一起。

intro.en: Imperil is built on the noun peril with the Latin prefix in-, and its family includes perilous and imperilment.
intro.cn: imperil 以名词 peril 为词基，加上拉丁语前缀 in- 构成，同族词有 perilous 与 imperilment。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun periculum means a trial or danger, and supplies both peril and the root of imperil.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 periculum 意为试验或危险，是 peril 与 imperil 共同的来源。

items.example: In- makes a noun into a verb of entering a state.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 把名词变成「进入某状态」的动词。

items.example: Periculum carries the idea of testing one luck.
items.exampleCN: periculum 隐含「拿运气去试」的意思。

items.example: The -culum suffix shapes periculum.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -culum 构成了 periculum。

items.example: Periclitari joins periculum to a verb ending.
items.exampleCN: periclitari 是 periculum 加动词词尾的形式。

items.example: Peril is the borrowed form of periculum.
items.exampleCN: peril 是 periculum 借入英语的形式。

items.example: The -ous suffix gives perilous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 perilous。

items.example: Perilous describes a crossing in a storm.
items.exampleCN: perilous 可以形容暴风雨中的渡航。

items.meaning: matching the d of the root
items.meaningCN: 与词尾 d 拼合，形成 -led 拼写
items.example: The -ed forms give imperilled and imperiled.
items.exampleCN: 过去式形成 imperilled 与 imperiled 两种拼写。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The -ment suffix forms imperilment.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 构成 imperilment。

items.example: The -ing form gives imperilling or imperiling.
items.exampleCN: 现在分词形成 imperilling 或 imperiling。

items.example: The -s form is imperils.
items.exampleCN: 第三人称单数形式是 imperils。

definition_zh: 假扮；冒充；扮演（某人）；拟人化
definition_en: to pretend to be someone else, usually to deceive people, or to copy a voice or manner for entertainment
core_image: 一个人戴上面具，换上别人的衣着与声音
scene: 电话那头的人自称是银行客服。The caller was arrested for impersonating a bank officer.
sceneCN: 这里 impersonate 是「冒充」（第 2 个义项：为欺骗而假装成别人）；句意：那名来电者因冒充银行职员而被捕。

pos.zh: 扮演；模仿（某人的举止腔调）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「冒充；扮演」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「模仿者；冒名者」
单词的词基，义为「人；个人」
去掉前缀 im- 的形式，义为「扮演；冒充」，多见于法律与旧时用语

senses.title: To pretend to be another person
senses.definition: to behave as if you were someone else, dressing and speaking in their way
senses.definitionCN: 表现得像另一个人，用对方的穿着和说话方式出现
senses.example: In the play she impersonates an ageing queen.
senses.exampleCN: 在剧中她假扮一位年迈的女王。
senses.why: The word is built from in- plus person, so the core picture is stepping into a person shape that is not your own.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 in- 加 person（人）构成，核心画面就是把自己塞进一个不属于自己的「人」的形状里，所以最早的义项是「假扮别人」。

senses.title: To assume an identity to deceive
senses.definition: to take on another person identity or official role in order to deceive or cheat
senses.definitionCN: 为欺骗或行骗而冒用他人的身份或公职
senses.example: He was fined for impersonating a police officer.
senses.exampleCN: 他因冒充警察而被罚款。
senses.why: Once someone wears another identity, the word links to fraud and crime, because the pretense causes real harm.
senses.whyCN: 既然有人戴上了别人的身份，这个词就与欺诈、犯罪挂上钩，因为这种假扮会造成实际伤害，于是从「扮演」转向「冒充」。

senses.title: To mimic for entertainment
senses.definition: to copy the voice, gestures, or mannerisms of a well-known person to amuse an audience
senses.definitionCN: 为取悦观众而模仿名人的嗓音、动作或习惯
senses.example: He can impersonate three famous actors perfectly.
senses.exampleCN: 他能把三位著名演员模仿得惟妙惟肖。
senses.why: Mimicry borrows the same person-stepping image without any deception, so the word also names harmless comic performance.
senses.whyCN: 模仿借用了同一个「变成某人」的画面，却不含欺骗，于是这个词也指无害的幽默表演，这是从「冒充」分出的另一支。

senses.title: To give human form to something
senses.definition: to represent a thing or idea as a person, especially in art
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术中把事物或观念表现为一个人
senses.example: The statue impersonates justice as a blindfolded woman.
senses.exampleCN: 这座雕像以蒙眼女子拟人化地表现正义。
senses.why: Since person is at the centre of the word, it can also mean giving a non-human thing a human face.
senses.whyCN: 既然 person（人）是这个词的核心，它自然也能表示「给非人的事物一张人的脸」，即拟人化。

intro.en: Impersonate is a learned English verb built from the prefix im-, into, the Latin word persona, a mask or a character, and the verb suffix -ate.
intro.cn: impersonate 是英语仿拉丁构词：前缀 im-（进入）+ 拉丁语 persona（面具、角色）+ 动词后缀 -ate。

items.en: Persona shifts from a mask in a play to a role and then to a human being.
items.cn: persona 从戏剧面具转而指角色，再指人。

items.en: Persona is the origin of the English word person and of its idea of a face worn before others.
items.cn: persona 是英语 person 的来源，也带着「在人前戴的面孔」的意味。

items.en: English personate, from Latin persona and -ate, appears in the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪由 persona 加 -ate 造出 personate。

items.en: The form impersonate is recorded in the early seventeenth century and spreads as impersonation.
items.cn: impersonate 这一形式在十七世纪前期见于书面，并随 impersonation 一词流传。

items.en: The sense broadens to professional mimicry of voices and stage characters.
items.cn: 十九世纪词义扩展为职业性的声音模仿与舞台角色扮演。

items.en: Modern use splits into legal fraud, online identity theft, and harmless performance.
items.cn: 现代用法分为法律上的欺诈、网络身份盗用与无害的表演三个方向。

note.en: Impersonate grows out of person and persona, and its neighbours divide between identity fraud and harmless mimicry.
note.cn: impersonate 由 person 与 persona 生长而来，近邻词分为身份欺诈与无害模仿两类。

entries.definition: the act of pretending to be someone else
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「冒充；扮演」

entries.definition: a person who imitates someone else
entries.definitionCN: 由动词加 -or 构成，义为「模仿者；冒名者」

entries.definition: to play a role or assume a character
entries.definitionCN: 去前缀形式，义为「扮演；冒充」，常用于法律

entries.definition: the mask or image a person presents to others
entries.definitionCN: 同源名词，义为「人格面具；形象」

entries.definition: to copy the way someone speaks or behaves
entries.definitionCN: 模仿某人的言行

entries.definition: to copy someone, often to make others laugh
entries.definitionCN: 模仿，常为逗人发笑

entries.definition: to pretend to be someone else under a false appearance
entries.definitionCN: 伪装；化装成他人

entries.definition: to behave as if something is true when it is not
entries.definitionCN: 假装；最宽泛的通用词

normalIntro.en: Impersonate means to get into a person: im- plus person plus the verb ending -ate.
normalIntro.cn: impersonate 就是钻进一个人的壳里：im- 加 person，再加动词后缀 -ate。

normal.en: The verb splits as im- plus person plus -ate, and person also gives personality.
normal.cn: 这个动词可拆成 im- + person + -ate，而 person 也是 personality 的词基。

normal.en: The -or suffix makes impersonator, and the -ion suffix makes impersonation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -or 构成 impersonator，后缀 -ion 构成 impersonation。

normal.en: The usual object is a role or an official: an officer, a celebrity, a doctor.
normal.cn: 常见宾语是身份或公职：官员、名人、医生。

normal.en: The passive be fined for impersonating is a standard news pattern.
normal.cn: 「因冒充……而被罚款」的被动句式是常见的新闻搭配。

normal.en: Compare imitate: imitate copies actions, impersonate takes on a whole person.
normal.cn: 对比 imitate：imitate 只模仿动作，impersonate 则是整个人「变成」某个人。

abstract.en: Picture a theatre mask held up to cover a face.
abstract.cn: 想象一张戏面具被举起来挡住真实的脸。

abstract.en: Imagine a badge and a borrowed uniform that do not quite fit.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚警徽和一套不太合身的借来的制服。

abstract.en: Think of a comic on stage copying a famous voice, word for word.
abstract.cn: 想象一位喜剧演员在台上，一字一句地复制名人的嗓音。

examples.en: The thief impersonated a delivery worker to enter the building.
examples.cn: 小偷冒充快递员进入大楼。

examples.en: Comedians often impersonate politicians during election season.
examples.cn: 竞选季里，喜剧演员常模仿政客。

examples.en: She can impersonate her teacher very convincingly.
examples.cn: 她把老师模仿得惟妙惟肖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬把人捏特」——硬把别人捏成某个人的模样；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 im-（进入）+ persona（面具；角色；人）+ -ate（动词后缀）→ 英语 impersonate，核心义「钻进另一个人的身份里」。

sensesIntro.en: Impersonate starts from stepping into another person, splits into deceptive identity theft and harmless mimicry, and also reaches the artistic sense of giving a thing human form.
sensesIntro.cn: impersonate 先是「钻进另一个人的身份」，然后分两支：骗人的冒名与无害的模仿，另外还延伸到艺术上的拟人化。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person wearing another person mask and voice.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人戴上了别人的面具、换上了别人的声音。

branches.en: The base sense is pretending to be someone else in dress and speech.
branches.cn: 基础义项是在衣着与言谈上假扮他人。

branches.en: When the pretense is for gain, the word means identity fraud.
branches.cn: 假扮带有获利目的时，这个词就指身份欺诈。

branches.en: Without deception, the same person-stepping image becomes comic mimicry.
branches.cn: 不含欺骗时，同一个「变成某人」的画面就变成滑稽模仿。

branches.en: Art can give a non-human idea a human face.
branches.cn: 艺术可以给非人的观念一张人的脸。

branches.en: Both walking on stage as another person and presenting a virtue as a woman take things beyond their own form.
branches.cn: 以他人身份登台，和把一种美德表现为女子，都是让事物越出自己的形态。

intro.en: Impersonate is centred on the Latin word persona, and the English family includes person, impersonator, and impersonation.
intro.cn: impersonate 以拉丁语 persona 为中心，英语同族词包括 person、impersonator、impersonation。

latinIntro.en: Latin persona first names a theatrical mask, then a character, then a human being, which is exactly how impersonate works.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 persona 先指戏剧面具，再指角色，最后指人，这正好解释了 impersonate 的用法。

items.example: The prefix im- shows stepping into a form.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 表示步入某种形态。

items.example: Persona supplies the middle of the word.
items.exampleCN: persona 提供这个词的中段。

items.example: The -ate suffix turns the noun into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 把名词变成动词。

items.example: Person is the everyday English reflex of persona.
items.exampleCN: person 是 persona 在英语中的日常形式。

items.example: Personate is the shorter legal cousin.
items.exampleCN: personate 是更简短的法律用词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词后缀
items.example: The -ion suffix forms impersonation.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 impersonation。

items.example: The -or suffix forms impersonator.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 构成 impersonator。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词后缀
items.example: The -ed form gives impersonated.
items.exampleCN: 过去式与过去分词为 impersonated。

items.example: The -ing form gives impersonating.
items.exampleCN: 现在分词为 impersonating。

items.example: The -s form is impersonates.
items.exampleCN: 第三人称单数为 impersonates。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 使声音透出；一般认为与 persona 有关

definition_zh: 不受影响的；无动于衷的；不透水的；不可渗透的
definition_en: not affected by something, or not allowing liquid, air, or another substance to pass through
core_image: 一层坚固的防水外套，雨水打在表面立刻滑走，里面始终干燥
scene: 暴雨中，登山者的风雨衣把雨水全部挡在外面。The hiker walked through the storm in a jacket that stayed impervious to the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 impervious 是「不透水的、不可渗透的」（第 3 个义项：液体或气体无法穿过）；句意：登山者穿过暴风雨，那件衣服始终挡得住雨水。

pos.zh: 不受影响的；无动于衷的

collocations.zh: 顶得住压力；不受压力影响

derivatives.zh: impervious 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「不受影响地；无动于衷地」
impervious 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「不透性；不受影响的状态」
去掉否定前缀 im- 后的肯定形，义为「可渗入的；能通过的」

senses.title: Not affected by something
senses.definition: not influenced or harmed by something such as criticism, pressure, or emotion
senses.definitionCN: 不受批评、压力、情感等事物影响或伤害的
senses.example: She seemed impervious to their criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 她对他们的批评似乎无动于衷。
senses.why: Latin per- means through, so im- + pervious means cannot be passed through, and an impervious mind lets words pass by without being touched.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 per- 意为「穿过」，所以 im- 加 pervious 表示「穿不过去」；不受影响的心让话语滑过去而毫无触动。

senses.title: Not admitting a substance
senses.definition: not allowing wind, gas, or heat to pass in or out
senses.definitionCN: 不让风、气体或热量进出或穿透的
senses.example: The tent is impervious to wind and damp.
senses.exampleCN: 这顶帐篷不透风，也不透潮气。
senses.why: The physical image of a surface that nothing can pierce extends from liquid to wind, gas, and heat.
senses.whyCN: 「什么都穿不过去」的物理画面从液体扩展到风、气体和热量，就产生了这个义项。

senses.title: Not letting water through
senses.definition: not letting water or another liquid pass through
senses.definitionCN: 不让水或其他液体通过的
senses.example: The coating makes the fabric impervious to water.
senses.exampleCN: 这层涂层让布料不透水。
senses.why: The literal meaning is the oldest: a material that water cannot pass through keeps its inner side dry.
senses.whyCN: 字面义是最早的用法：水流不过去的材料，把内侧始终保持在干燥状态。

senses.title: Hard to change or reach
senses.definition: too fixed in attitude or belief to be changed or reached by argument
senses.definitionCN: 态度或信念过于固定，无法被说服改变的
senses.example: The old council was impervious to reason.
senses.exampleCN: 那个旧议会听不进任何道理。
senses.why: If nothing can pass through a surface, then no argument can pass into the mind behind it, and the person becomes unyielding.
senses.whyCN: 如果什么都穿不过表面，那么任何道理也进不了背后的头脑，人于是变得固执不化。

intro.en: Impervious joins the negative prefix im- to Latin pervius, meaning passable, which in turn comes from per, through, and via, way.
intro.cn: impervious 由否定前缀 im- 加上拉丁语 pervius（可通行的）构成，而 pervius 又来自 per（穿过）与 via（道路）。

items.en: Via means a way or a road.
items.cn: via 意为道路、通道。

items.en: Pervius describes something that can be crossed or passed through.
items.cn: pervius 形容可以横穿或通过的东西。

items.en: Scholar Latin forms impervius as the direct negative.
items.cn: 学术拉丁语构成 impervius 作为直接否定形。

items.en: Early modern writers borrow the word as a technical adjective.
items.cn: 近代早期写作者借入这个词，用作技术性形容词。

items.en: Modern English extends it from unpassable roads to matter that resists water and to minds that resist influence.
items.cn: 现代英语把它从「走不通的路」扩展到抗水的材料，以及抗拒影响的头脑。

note.en: Impervious is built from Latin via, a road: first something that cannot be passed through, then a mind that cannot be touched or shifted.
note.cn: impervious 来自拉丁语 via（道路）：先指「穿不过去的东西」，再指「触动不了、推不动的头脑」。

entries.definition: allowing something to pass through
entries.definitionCN: 可渗透的；能通过的

entries.definition: not allowing liquid to pass through
entries.definitionCN: 不可渗透的；不透水的

entries.definition: not aware of what is happening
entries.definitionCN: 浑然不觉的（只是拼写与音近，词源不同）

entries.definition: not influenced or changed by something
entries.definitionCN: 不受影响的

entries.definition: that water cannot pass through
entries.definitionCN: 防水的

entries.definition: too slow to feel or respond to what matters
entries.definitionCN: 麻木的；感觉迟钝的

normalIntro.en: Impervious is im- plus pervious: nothing can go through the surface and reach what lies behind it.
normalIntro.cn: impervious 是 im- 加 pervious：什么也穿不过表面，到达不了后面。

normal.en: Im- makes a word negative, as in impossible and impatient.
normal.cn: im- 表示否定，如 impossible、impatient。

normal.en: Latin via means road, and pervious means able to be crossed, so an impervious surface is one no way passes through.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 via 是道路，pervious 是可通行的，所以 impervious 表面无路可通。

normal.en: Impervious to criticism is a common pairing for someone who ignores objections.
normal.cn: impervious to criticism 常用来形容无视反对意见的人。

normal.en: Scientists say cities have impervious surfaces such as roads and car parks, where rain cannot soak in.
normal.cn: 科学家称城市里的道路、停车场是不透水面，雨水无法渗入。

normal.en: Compare waterproof: waterproof names rain and cloth, while impervious is broader and also covers influence.
normal.cn: 对比 waterproof：waterproof 多用于雨和布料，impervious 范围更广，还覆盖影响力。

abstract.en: Picture a raincoat that drops every bead of water without getting wet.
abstract.cn: 想象一件雨衣，水珠颗颗落下，衣料却始终干爽。

abstract.en: Imagine words hitting a thick glass wall and sliding away.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵厚厚的玻璃墙，话语撞上去就滑开了。

abstract.en: Think of a stone road that rain can fall on but never sink into.
abstract.cn: 想象一条石路，雨落在上面却渗不进去。

examples.en: The new tyres are impervious to mud and rain.
examples.cn: 新轮胎不怕泥泞和雨淋。

examples.en: He remained impervious to all advice from his colleagues.
examples.cn: 他对同事们的所有建议都充耳不闻。

examples.en: Concrete paving creates impervious surfaces that increase flooding.
examples.cn: 混凝土铺装形成的不透水地面会加剧洪水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬皮尔维尔斯」——硬得皮都扒不开，水进不去，也就不受影响；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语前缀 im-（不）+ per（穿过）+ via（道路）→ pervius（可通行的）→ 拉丁 impervius（走不通的）→ 英语 impervious，核心义「穿不过去」。

sensesIntro.en: Impervious starts from a surface that nothing can pass through, and that image spreads to water, to wind and heat, and finally to a mind that no argument can reach.
sensesIntro.cn: impervious 从「什么都穿不过去」的表面出发，这一画面扩展到水、风与热，最后落到「任何道理也进不去」的头脑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rainproof coat from which every drop slides away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件雨衣，雨点沿着表面滑走。

branches.en: Being unmoved by criticism comes from the sealed surface.
branches.cn: 不受批评影响，来自封闭的表面。

branches.en: Wind, gas, and heat cannot cross the barrier.
branches.cn: 风、气体与热量都无法越过屏障。

branches.en: Waterproofing is the most literal sense.
branches.cn: 防水是最字面的义项。

branches.en: A closed mind is stubbornness built on the same image.
branches.cn: 闭塞的头脑是建立在同一画面上的固执。

branches.en: Both senses describe resistance to outside influence.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在描述对外界影响的抵抗。

intro.en: Impervious is built from im-, the Latin prefix for not, plus Latin via, a road, with per- meaning through.
intro.cn: impervious 由 im-（拉丁语否定前缀）、per-（穿过）与 via（道路）构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin via means a road, and pervius means passable, so impervius means having no way through.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 via 意为道路，pervius 意为可通行的，所以 impervius 表示没有通道可走。

items.example: The prefix im- turns pervious into its negative.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 把 pervious 变成否定形。

items.example: Per- appears in pervious and permeate.
items.exampleCN: per- 出现在 pervious 与 permeate 中。

items.example: Via is the root of devious and trivial.
items.exampleCN: via 是 devious 与 trivial 的词根。

items.example: Pervius literally means that has a way through.
items.exampleCN: pervius 字面意思就是有一条路可通。

items.example: The suffix -ous turns pervius into an English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 使 pervius 成为英语形容词。

items.example: Impervius is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: impervius 是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms imperviously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 imperviously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms imperviousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 imperviousness。

items.example: The suffix -able forms the partner word impermeable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成同族词 impermeable。

definition_zh: 冲动的；鲁莽的；急躁的；猛烈的
definition_en: acting quickly and suddenly without thinking carefully, or moving with great and violent force
core_image: 一个人不等门打开就一头撞过去，像洪水冲垮堤坝一样停不下来
scene: 争论还没结束，他就拍桌子站起来做出决定。Angry and impetuous, he decided before hearing the other side.
sceneCN: 这里 impetuous 是「冲动的、不假思索就行动的」（第 2 个义项：行事急躁、不加考虑）；句意：他怒气冲天、做事冲动，还没听完另一方的说法就下了决定。

derivatives.zh: 由 impetuous 加拉丁名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「冲动；鲁莽」
impetuous 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「冲动地；鲁莽地」
impetuous 加后缀 -ness 构成，义为「冲动、急躁的性质」
与 impetuous 同出拉丁 impetere，义为「推动力；冲劲」

senses.title: Charging forward with force
senses.definition: moving or acting with sudden and great force
senses.definitionCN: 以突然而巨大的力量前进或行动的
senses.example: An impetuous wave broke over the rocks.
senses.exampleCN: 一股猛浪冲过岩石。
senses.why: Latin impetere means to rush against, so the earliest image is a body or a river hurled forward at full speed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 impetere 意为「冲向」，最早的形象是身体或河流以全速向前猛冲。

senses.title: Acting without thinking
senses.definition: doing things quickly and suddenly without pausing to think
senses.definitionCN: 做事迅速突然，不停下来考虑的
senses.example: His impetuous decision cost him the job.
senses.exampleCN: 他一时的冲动决定让他丢了工作。
senses.why: A person who moves on impulse is like a body launched forward, with no pause for judgement.
senses.whyCN: 凭一时冲动行事的人，就像被抛出去的身体，没有停下来判断的时刻。

senses.title: Quick to anger
senses.definition: having a hasty, hot temper with little patience
senses.definitionCN: 脾气急躁、缺乏耐心的
senses.example: The impetuous coach shouted at the referee.
senses.exampleCN: 急躁的教练冲裁判大喊。
senses.why: Sudden forward motion passes into the temper itself: the mind rushes ahead before the calm part can catch up.
senses.whyCN: 「突然前冲」由动作转到性情上：头脑抢先冲出去，冷静的那部分还没来得及跟上。

senses.title: Violent natural motion
senses.definition: describing wind, water, or weather that moves violently and fast
senses.definitionCN: 形容风、水或天气猛烈而迅速地运动的
senses.example: The boat was driven by an impetuous wind.
senses.exampleCN: 小船被一阵狂风推着走。
senses.why: The literal force of the Latin verb survives in descriptions of moving elements of nature.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词的字面力量在描写自然元素运动时保留了下来。

intro.en: Impetuous comes from Latin impetuosus, from impetus, a rush or attack, from impetere, to rush upon.
intro.cn: impetuous 来自拉丁语 impetuosus，源自动名词 impetus（猛冲、攻击），而 impetus 又来自 impetere（冲向）。

items.en: Petere means to seek, aim at, or attack.
items.cn: petere 意为寻求、瞄准或攻击。

items.en: Impetere combines in- with petere to mean rush upon.
items.cn: impetere 由 in- 与 petere 组合，意为扑向、冲向。

items.en: Impetus is the noun for a rush or an attack.
items.cn: impetus 表示猛冲或攻击的名词。

items.en: Impetueux carries the adjective into Old French.
items.cn: impetueux 把形容词带入古法语。

items.en: English borrows impetuous, first for violent motion, then for hasty temper.
items.cn: 英语借入 impetuous，先指猛烈运动，后指急躁性情。

note.en: Impetuous comes from impetere, to rush upon, and shares its family with impetus, a driving force.
note.cn: impetuous 来自 impetere（冲向），与表示推动力的 impetus 属于同一个词族。

entries.definition: a force that pushes something forward
entries.definitionCN: 推动力；促进因素

entries.definition: expecting to be obeyed
entries.definitionCN: 专横的；傲慢的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: the quality of acting on impulse
entries.definitionCN: 冲动；鲁莽

entries.definition: acting without thought of the result
entries.definitionCN: 轻率的；鲁莽的

entries.definition: acting on a sudden urge
entries.definitionCN: 冲动的

entries.definition: done too quickly and too soon
entries.definitionCN: 匆忙的；草率的

normalIntro.en: Impetuous is the Latin rush: in- plus petere, to go at something, turned into a temper that never waits.
normalIntro.cn: impetuous 就是拉丁语的「猛冲」：in- 加 petere（扑向），变成一种从不等一等的性情。

normal.en: The Latin verb petere gives our words petition and compete, as well as this rushing root.
normal.cn: 拉丁动词 petere 既衍生出 petition、compete，也衍生出这个「猛冲」词根。

normal.en: Impetus, a force that drives something forward, is the closest cousin of impetuous.
normal.cn: impetus 指推动力，是 impetuous 最亲近的同族词。

normal.en: The noun form impetuosity is used for a person who keeps leaping before looking.
normal.cn: 名词 impetuosity 用来形容不断事后再想的人。

normal.en: Writers pair impetuous with youth, because young age is often called hasty.
normal.cn: 作者常把 impetuous 与 youth 搭配，因为年轻常被说成急躁。

normal.en: Note the spelling change from impetus: the English adjective adds the Latin ending -uous to a stem that ends in -u.
normal.cn: 注意与 impetus 的拼写差别：英语形容词在词干后加拉丁词尾 -uous。

abstract.en: Picture a rider whipping the horse before the gate is even open.
abstract.cn: 想象闸门还没开，骑手就抽打马匹向前冲。

abstract.en: Imagine a river bursting through a broken dam.
abstract.cn: 想象河水从溃开的堤坝冲出去。

abstract.en: Think of a finger pressing the reply button before the sentence is read twice.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话还没读第二遍，手指已经按下了回复键。

examples.en: Her impetuous offer to help surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 她冲动地提出帮忙，让所有人都很吃惊。

examples.en: An impetuous driver is a danger to the whole road.
examples.cn: 鲁莽的司机对整条道路都是威胁。

examples.en: The impetuous current swept the swimmers downstream.
examples.cn: 湍急的水流把游泳者冲向下游。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬拍锤子」——不等细看就硬拍下去，像锤子一样冲动；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内、对着）+ petere（冲向）→ impetere（猛扑）→ impetus（猛冲）→ impetuosus → 英语 impetuous，核心义「一头冲过去」。

sensesIntro.en: Impetuous begins with a body that charges forward, then names the person who acts on such force, the hot temper behind it, and finally the violent motion of wind and water.
sensesIntro.cn: impetuous 先指向前猛冲的身体，再指凭这股力量行事的人、背后的火爆脾气，最后指风与水的猛烈运动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body charging into a closed gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：一具身体朝关着的门冲过去。

branches.en: The literal rush is the physical core.
branches.cn: 字面上的猛冲是物理核心。

branches.en: The rush becomes a habit of acting without pausing.
branches.cn: 猛冲变成不加停顿就行动的习性。

branches.en: A rushing mind shows itself as a quick temper.
branches.cn: 猛冲的头脑表现为急脾气。

branches.en: Wind and water keep the oldest literal sense.
branches.cn: 风与水保留了最古老的字面义。

branches.en: A charging body and a violent storm share the same impetere root.
branches.cn: 冲撞的身体与暴烈的风雨共享同一个词根。

intro.en: Impetuous joins Latin in- with petere, meaning to seek or to rush at, and adds the ending -ous.
intro.cn: impetuous 由拉丁语 in-、petere（寻求、扑向）与词尾 -ous 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere means to seek or attack, and impetere means to rush upon, giving both impetuous and impetus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 petere 意为寻求或攻击，impetere 意为扑向，由此得到 impetuous 与 impetus。

items.example: The prefix im- here means towards, not not.
items.exampleCN: 这里前缀 im- 表示朝向，而不是否定。

items.example: Petere also gives petition and repeat.
items.exampleCN: petere 也衍生出 petition 与 repeat。

items.example: Impetere is the source of impetuous.
items.exampleCN: impetere 是 impetuous 的来源。

items.example: Impetus survives as an English noun for driving force.
items.exampleCN: impetus 作为表示推动力的英语名词保留下来。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ous 构成这个英语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms impetuosity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 impetuosity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms impetuously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 impetuously。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms impetuousness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 impetuousness。

items.example: Impetuous keeps the rushing core.
items.exampleCN: impetuous 保留了「猛冲」核心。

definition_zh: 推动力；促进因素；冲劲；动量
definition_en: a force or reason that makes something happen, grow, or move faster, or the momentum of a moving body
core_image: 一只手在巨石的背后猛地一推，石头开始滚动并越滚越快
scene: 新出台的奖学金政策让更多学生愿意攻读科研。The new scholarship gave a real impetus to scientific study.
sceneCN: 这里 impetus 是「促进因素、推动力」（第 3 个义项：使某事发展或更有进展的力量）；句意：新奖学金给科学研究带来了实实在在的推动力。

derivatives.zh: 与 impetus 同出拉丁 impetere，义为「冲动的；猛烈的」
由 impetuous 加 -ity 构成，义为「冲动；鲁莽」
由 impetuous 加 -ly 构成，义为「冲动地」

senses.title: A push that moves a body
senses.definition: the force with which a moving body is pushed forward
senses.definitionCN: 使运动物体向前推进的力量
senses.example: The ball rolled down the slope under its own impetus.
senses.exampleCN: 球靠着自身的冲力沿坡滚下。
senses.why: Latin impetus is the noun of impetere, to rush upon, and first names the physical force of a body thrown forward.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 impetus 是 impetere（冲向）的名词形式，最初指物体向前抛出时的物理力量。

senses.title: Momentum that keeps building
senses.definition: the momentum that keeps something moving once it has started
senses.definitionCN: 事物一旦开始便持续前进的势头
senses.example: The campaign gained impetus after the debate.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论之后，这场运动声势越来越大。
senses.why: From the force of a single push the word moves to the speed and weight a moving thing carries onward.
senses.whyCN: 从一次推动产生的力量，词义转向物体向前携带的速度与重量感。

senses.title: A motivating force
senses.definition: something that encourages a process or activity to develop faster
senses.definitionCN: 促使某个过程或活动更快发展的事物
senses.example: Education is the strongest impetus for social change.
senses.exampleCN: 教育是社会变革最强大的推动力。
senses.why: An abstract event can push people the way a hand pushes a stone, so the physical force becomes a motive.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的事件可以像手推动石头一样推动人们，于是物理力量变成了动机。

senses.title: A driving aim
senses.definition: a strong desire that drives a person to act
senses.definitionCN: 驱使一个人行动的强烈愿望
senses.example: Curiosity was the impetus behind his research.
senses.exampleCN: 好奇心是他研究的动力。
senses.why: The same force is internalised as an aim that keeps a person moving in one direction.
senses.whyCN: 同一种力量内化为一个目标，使一个人持续朝同一方向前进。

senses.title: An urge of the mind
senses.definition: a sudden strong urge that carries a person along
senses.definitionCN: 突然而强烈的、把人带着往前走的冲动
senses.example: On a sudden impetus he stood up and spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 凭着一股突然的冲动，他站起来发言。
senses.why: The Latin noun also names an impulse of the mind, the same rushing energy turned inward.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁名词也指思绪上的冲动，是同一种猛冲的能量转向内心。

intro.en: Impetus is taken straight from Latin impetus, a rush or attack, the noun of impetere, to rush upon.
intro.cn: impetus 直接借自拉丁语 impetus（猛冲、攻击），是动词 impetere（冲向）的名词形式。

items.en: Petere means to seek or to attack.
items.cn: petere 意为寻求或攻击。

items.en: Impetere is in- plus petere, to rush upon something.
items.cn: impetere 是 in- 加 petere，意为扑向某物。

items.en: Impetus names the rush itself, later the force in a moving body.
items.cn: impetus 指猛冲本身，后来指运动物体中的力量。

items.en: English borrows the Latin word unchanged.
items.cn: 英语原样借入这个拉丁词。

items.en: Later it widens to mean momentum and any force that drives a process forward.
items.cn: 后来它扩展为动量，以及推动任何进程前进的力量。

note.en: Impetus is the Latin noun behind impetuous: a force that pushes a body, a plan, or a mind forward.
note.cn: impetus 是 impetuous 背后的拉丁名词：推动身体、计划或头脑向前的力量。

entries.definition: acting on sudden impulse
entries.definitionCN: 冲动的；鲁莽的

entries.definition: showing no respect for religion
entries.definitionCN: 不敬神的（拼写与音近，词源不同）

entries.definition: a skin infection
entries.definitionCN: 脓疱疮（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: force gained by movement or by a process
entries.definitionCN: 动量；势头

entries.definition: something that encourages activity
entries.definitionCN: 刺激物；激励因素
