normalIntro.en: Impetus is the Latin push: the noun of a verb that means to rush upon something.
normalIntro.cn: impetus 是拉丁语的「一推」：一个意为「扑向」的动词的名词形。

normal.en: Impetus and impetuous come from the same Latin verb impetere.
normal.cn: impetus 与 impetuous 来自同一个拉丁动词 impetere。

normal.en: Latin petere means to seek, and it also gives petition and appetite.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 petere 意为寻求，也衍生出 petition 与 appetite。

normal.en: The phrase give impetus to is the classic way to say push something forward.
normal.cn: 搭配 give impetus to 是表达「推动某事」的经典说法。

normal.en: Gain impetus and lose impetus describe how a movement speeds up or slows down.
normal.cn: gain impetus 与 lose impetus 描述一场运动如何加速或减速。

normal.en: In physics, impetus once meant the quantity of motion of a moving body, an early idea of momentum.
normal.cn: 在物理学中，impetus 曾指运动物体的运动量，是动量的早期概念。

abstract.en: Since drive and resistance are opposites, one hand on a heavy rock is enough for the whole word.
abstract.cn: 推与阻是一对相反的力量，一只手推着巨石就足以代表整个词。

abstract.en: Picture a runaway cart with nobody pushing: momentum keeps it going.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆无人推动却停不下的车：动量带着它前进。

abstract.en: Think of a spark that makes a crowd suddenly start moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火星让一群人突然行动起来。

examples.en: The new road gave an impetus to local trade.
examples.cn: 新公路推动了当地的贸易。

examples.en: The movement lost its impetus after the winter.
examples.cn: 这场运动在冬天之后失去了势头。

examples.en: Her early success provided the impetus to keep writing.
examples.cn: 她早年的成功给了她继续写作的动力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬皮椅子」——猛地一推，硬皮椅子就滑出去老远，这正是推动力；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（向内、对着）+ petere（冲向）→ impetere（猛扑）→ 名词 impetus（猛冲；动量）→ 英语 impetus，核心义「把人或事物推动起来的力量」。

sensesIntro.en: Impetus starts as the force of a moving body, becomes the momentum it carries, and then extends to any force or motive that pushes an event or a person forward.
sensesIntro.cn: impetus 先是运动物体的力量，然后变成它携带的动量，再扩展为推动事件或人前进的任何力量或动机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushing a boulder so that it starts to roll.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把巨石推动，让它开始滚动。

branches.en: The physical push is the first literal sense.
branches.cn: 物理上的推动是第一个字面义。

branches.en: Momentum is the push carried onward.
branches.cn: 动量是将推动带向远方。

branches.en: Social and economic forces borrow the same image.
branches.cn: 社会与经济的力量借用同一画面。

branches.en: A motive and an impulse are the internal versions.
branches.cn: 动机与冲动是它的内在版本。

branches.en: A single push and the motion it starts belong together.
branches.cn: 一次推动与它引发的运动密不可分。

intro.en: Impetus is the Latin noun of impetere, and English uses its family through impetuous and impetuosity.
intro.cn: impetus 是 impetere 的拉丁名词形，英语通过 impetuous 与 impetuosity 使用它的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin petere means to seek or attack, in- means towards, and impetus names the rush that follows.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 petere 意为寻求或攻击，in- 意为朝向，impetus 表示随之而来的猛冲。

items.example: The prefix im- turns to towards in this word.
items.exampleCN: 在这个词里前缀 im- 意为朝向。

items.example: Petere is also behind compete and petition.
items.exampleCN: compete 与 petition 也源自 petere。

items.example: Impetere gives the noun its meaning.
items.exampleCN: impetere 赋予了这个名词含义。

items.meaningCN: 拉丁第四变格名词词尾
items.example: The ending -us marks a Latin masculine noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -us 标记拉丁阳性名词。

items.example: Latin impetus enters English unchanged.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 impetus 原样进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -uous forms impetuous.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -uous 构成 impetuous。

items.example: The suffix -ity forms impetuosity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 impetuosity。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms impetuously.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 impetuously。

items.example: The plural impetuses follows the English pattern.
items.exampleCN: 复数 impetuses 遵循英语规则。

definition_zh: 牵涉；使卷入；暗示；影响
definition_en: to show that someone is involved in a crime or a wrongdoing, or to suggest something without saying it directly
core_image: 一根绳子从案发现场一路绕过来，套住了某个人的手腕
scene: 仓库里少了两箱货，监控拍到一个背影；顺着这条线索查下去，有个保安的名字被一再提到。A trail of evidence implicated the night guard in the theft.
sceneCN: 这里 implicate 是「牵涉、使卷入」（第 1 个义项：表明某人参与某件坏事）；句意为一条证据链把夜班保安牵涉进了这起盗窃案。绳套绕上手的那幅画面，就是这个词的核心印象。

pos.zh: 使卷入；牵涉；暗示；（对生物机能）有影响

derivatives.zh: implicat- 加 -ion 构成名词，义为「牵连」「含义」
分词转作形容词，义为「有牵连的、涉嫌的」
同词根 com- + plicare，义为「使复杂」
反向前缀 ex- + plicare，义为「详细解释」
同词根 du- + plicare，义为「复制」
形容词 simplex 加 -ity，义为「简单」

senses.title: To show that someone shares in a crime
senses.definition: to show or suggest that a person is involved in a crime or a wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 表明或暗示某人参与了罪行或不法行为
senses.example: The letters implicate two officials in the money-laundering scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 这些信件把两名官员牵涉进了洗钱计划。
senses.why: Latin plicare meant to fold, so the prefix in- folds a person into the case: once folded in, you are part of it and cannot stand outside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 plicare 意为「折叠」，前缀 in- 把某人折进案子里：一旦被折进去，就成了案子的一部分，再站不到外面去了。

senses.title: To hint at a cause without stating it
senses.definition: to suggest that something is probably true or probably the cause, without saying so openly
senses.definitionCN: 不明说却表示某事很可能是真的，或很可能是原因
senses.example: These results implicate diet in the rising rates of the disease.
senses.exampleCN: 这些结果暗示饮食与该病发病率上升有关。
senses.why: If folding something in means making it part of a case, the same fold can be made only in thought: an undisclosed link that the evidence quietly carries.
senses.whyCN: 既然把某物折进来就是让它成为案子的一部分，这种折也可以只发生在思路上：证据悄悄带出的一条没有明说的联系。

senses.title: To bring a thing into a matter
senses.definition: to connect a thing, such as a company or a place, with a problem or an event
senses.definitionCN: 把公司、地点等事物同某个问题或事件联系起来
senses.example: Two banks were implicated in the collapse of the fund.
senses.exampleCN: 两家银行被牵涉进了这只基金的崩盘。
senses.why: The fold does not choose between people and things: anyone or anything drawn into the case is implicated, whether or not the law is involved.
senses.whyCN: 这个「折」并不区分人与物：凡是被拉进事件里的，不管有没有法律介入，都叫 implicated。

senses.title: To affect the working of the body
senses.definition: to have an effect on a body system or a biological process
senses.definitionCN: 对身体系统或生物过程产生影响
senses.example: Chronic stress has been implicated in heart disease.
senses.exampleCN: 长期压力被认为与心脏病有关。
senses.why: Medical writing folds a factor into a disorder: the factor is not the disease, but it is part of the chain of causes.
senses.whyCN: 医学写作把一个因素折进某种疾病里：这个因素不是病本身，却是病因链条上的一环。

intro.en: Implicate comes from Latin implicare, to enfold or entangle, built from in- (into) and plicare (to fold), and passed through the Latin noun implicatio into English.
intro.cn: implicate 来自拉丁语 implicare（包裹、使纠缠），由 in-（进入）与 plicare（折叠）构成，再经拉丁语名词 implicatio 进入英语。

items.en: Plicare meant to fold, to bend or to lay in layers.
items.cn: plicare 意为折叠、弯曲、层层叠放。

items.en: Implicare meant to enfold something so that it was wrapped up in something else.
items.cn: implicare 意为把某物包起来，让它裹在另一物之中。

items.en: The noun implicatio gave the idea of an entanglement, a thing folded into a larger whole.
items.cn: 名词 implicatio 给出「纠缠、牵连」的观念：某物被折进一个更大的整体。

items.en: The verb entered English in the sense of entangling or entwining, first in writing about the body and the mind.
items.cn: 这个动词在十五、十六世纪进入英语，先表「纠缠、盘绕」，多用于谈论身体与心智的文字。

items.en: Legal and moral writing gave it the modern sense of bringing a person into a case or a guilt.
items.cn: 法律与道德写作赋予它现代义：把一个人牵进案子或罪责之中。

items.en: Modern medical and scientific writing extends it to any factor folded into a cause.
items.cn: 现代医学与科学写作把它扩展到任何被折进原因链里的因素。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the other plicare compounds, which all share the image of folding; the near-meaning group gathers words of involving, of hinting and of accusing.
note.cn: 形近组收其他 plicare 复合词，它们都共享「折叠」的意象；近义组收表示「卷入」「暗示」和「指控」的词。

entries.definition: to make something harder to understand, from com- plus plicare, to fold together
entries.definitionCN: 同词根词，com- 加 plicare「折在一起」，义为「使复杂」。

entries.definition: to unfold a meaning and explain it, with ex- meaning out
entries.definitionCN: 同词根词，ex- 表「向外」，义为「展开解释」；与 implicate 的「折进去」方向相反。

entries.definition: to make an exact copy, from duo plus plicare, folded twice
entries.definitionCN: 同词根词，duo 加 plicare「折了两折」，义为「复制」。

entries.definition: the noun of implicate, meaning an involvement or an unstated meaning
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「牵连」或「言外之意」。

entries.definition: to include someone in an activity or a situation; broader and more neutral
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「使参与、包含」，范围更广、更中性；implicate 通常带负面色彩。

entries.definition: to make someone seem guilty of a crime
entries.definitionCN: 法律用语，义为「使显示有罪」；比 implicate 更强调罪责。

entries.definition: to say openly that someone has done wrong
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「公开指控」；implicate 只是显示牵连，未必明说。

entries.definition: to put forward an idea without stating it firmly
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「表明、暗示」，用于第 2 个义项的「不带明说的提示」。

normalIntro.en: Implicate is built from the Latin verb for folding, so these hooks all turn on the picture of something being folded into a case.
normalIntro.cn: implicate 由拉丁语「折叠」动词构成，所以下面的记忆钩子都围绕「把某物折进一个案子里」的画面展开。

normal.en: im- means into and plicare means to fold: to unfold the case is explicate, to fold someone into it is implicate.
normal.cn: im- 意为「进入」，plicare 意为「折叠」：把事情摊开解释是 explicate，把人折进案子里就是 implicate。

normal.en: The noun implication carries two senses at once: an involvement and an unstated meaning.
normal.cn: 名词 implication 同时带两个义项：「牵连」与「言外之意」。

normal.en: In crime reporting, a suspect is implicated in a case; the passive form is by far the most common.
normal.cn: 在犯罪报道里，嫌疑人「被牵涉进」案子；被动式 be implicated in 是最常见的用法。

normal.en: Medical and scientific writing uses it for causes: a gene or a habit is implicated in a disease.
normal.cn: 医学与科学写作里它指原因：某个基因或某种习惯被认为与某种病有关。

normal.en: Compare involve: involve simply includes, while implicate usually suggests something doubtful or guilty.
normal.cn: 对比 involve：involve 只是「包含、参与」，implicate 通常暗示可疑或有罪。

abstract.en: Picture a long rope lying in the dust, one end tied to a case file and the other looped around a wrist.
abstract.cn: 想象一根长绳落在灰里，一头系着卷宗，另一头绕过某人的手腕。

abstract.en: Picture a hand quietly pushing a folded note under a folder marked for a different case, without saying a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手悄悄把一张折好的纸条塞进另一个卷宗的文件夹里，什么也不说。

abstract.en: Picture a name written on a sheet of paper that is slowly folded in with the others: the crease runs straight through it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个名字写在纸上，被慢慢和其他纸折在一起：折痕正压着它穿过。

examples.en: The emails implicated the manager in the fraud.
examples.cn: 这些邮件把经理牵涉进了这起欺诈案。

examples.en: Recent studies implicate sleep loss in weight gain.
examples.cn: 近期研究暗示睡眠不足与体重增加有关。

examples.en: She refused to implicate her colleagues in the scandal.
examples.cn: 她拒绝把同事牵连进这桩丑闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「隐不离扣」——被暗地里（隐）扣住、扣进了案子里，就是牵涉；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（进入）+ plicare（折叠）→ implicare（包裹、使纠缠）→ implicatio → 英语 implicate，核心义「把某人某物折进事件之中」；同族有 complicate、explicate、duplicate、simplicity。

sensesIntro.en: Implicate always folds something into a larger whole: first a person folded into a crime, then a cause folded into a disease or a problem, and finally a quiet hint that the fold exists.
sensesIntro.cn: implicate 一直在做同一件事：把某物折进更大的整体里。先是一个人被折进罪案，再是一个原因被折进疾病或问题，最后是不明说、只让人感觉到那道折痕的存在。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rope comes round from a scene and loops around a wrist.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根绳子从现场一路绕过来，套住了某人的手腕。

branches.en: The legal branch: evidence folds a person into a crime.
branches.cn: 法律分支：证据把一个人折进罪案里。

branches.en: The hinting branch: a link is folded in but never stated aloud.
branches.cn: 暗示分支：联系被折进去了，却从不被说出口。

branches.en: The object branch: companies and places are folded in just like people.
branches.cn: 事物分支：公司、地点与人一样会被折进事件。

branches.en: The body branch: a factor is folded into the chain of a disease.
branches.cn: 身体分支：某个因素被折进疾病的因果链。

branches.en: The shared branch: in both senses something is carried invisibly inside the case.
branches.cn: 共同分支：两个义项里都有某样东西被无声地装在事件之中。

intro.en: Implicate is a Latin verb of folding with a Latin prefix; English adds the usual verb endings and builds the noun implication, and the same root runs through complicate and explicate.
intro.cn: implicate 是一个带拉丁前缀的「折叠」动词；英语加上寻常动词词尾，又造出名词 implication，同一词根还贯穿 complicate 与 explicate。

latinIntro.en: Latin in- means into and plicare means to fold; implicare is recorded, and the noun implicatio is its direct descendant.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语前缀 in- 意为「进入」，plicare 意为「折叠」；implicare 有文献记录，名词 implicatio 是它的直接衍生。

items.example: The prefix marks a movement inward, into a whole.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记向内、进入一个整体。

items.example: The root carries the picture of something folded in layers.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根带着层层折叠的画面。

items.example: The verb is the folding root itself.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词就是「折叠」词根本身。

items.example: The prefix and the root joined to mean to enfold.
items.exampleCN: 前缀与词根合成「包裹」之义。

items.example: The ending forms the English verb implicate.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成英语动词 implicate。

items.meaningCN: 表示已受到的动作或状态
items.example: It forms implicated, often used in the passive.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 implicated，常用于被动式。

items.example: It forms implicating.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 implicating。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix turns implicat- into implication.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 implicat- 变成 implication。

items.example: With ex- the folding goes the other way: explicate unfolds.
items.exampleCN: 加上 ex-，折的方向反过来：explicate 是「摊开」。

items.example: With com- things are folded together: complicate.
items.exampleCN: 加上 com-，东西被折在一起：complicate。

definition_zh: 无力；无能；（医学上）阳痿；束手无策
definition_en: the lack of power to act, to change things or, in medical use, to have sexual intercourse
core_image: 一个人用力推一扇沉重的门，门却纹丝不动
scene: 老屋的木门被时间咬坏了，推一下晃一下，却怎么也推不开。He felt a deep impotence as the floodwater crept into the house.
sceneCN: 这里 impotence 是「无力感、束手无策」（第 1 个义项：想做却做不了的无能为力）；句意为洪水渐渐漫进屋子时，他感到一种深深的无力。推不动门的那幅画面，就是这个词的核心印象。

pos.zh: 名词：无力；无能；（医学上）阳痿

derivatives.zh: in- 加 potens「有力的」构成形容词，义为「无力的；无能的」
去掉否定前缀的肯定形式，义为「强有力的；有效的」
同源，义为「潜在的」，指藏着而尚未发挥的力量
potent 加 -cy 构成名词，义为「效力；力量」

senses.title: A lack of power to act
senses.definition: the state of being unable to act or to change a situation, especially one that is painful or unjust
senses.definitionCN: 无法行动或无法改变局面的状态，尤指面对痛苦或不公之时
senses.example: The villagers watched the drought with a growing sense of impotence.
senses.exampleCN: 村民们看着旱情，无力感越来越重。
senses.why: The prefix in- denies the Latin potent- of power, so impotence is literally a state with no power at all: the door stays shut whatever the hand does.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了拉丁语中「有力」的 potent-，所以 impotence 字面上就是一种完全没有力量的状态：手再用力，门也不动。

senses.title: A weakness of body or of will
senses.definition: physical weakness, or a lack of strength in an organ or a limb
senses.definitionCN: 体力上的虚弱，或器官、肢体力量的缺失
senses.example: Illness left him in a state of utter impotence.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病使他陷入了完全虚弱的状态。
senses.why: When the missing power is physical, the same denial of power moves from a feeling about the world to the body itself.
senses.whyCN: 当缺失的力量落在身体上，这种否定就从「对世界无能为力」转到了肉体本身。

senses.title: A failure to produce results
senses.definition: the failure of a policy, an action or a threat to achieve what it aims at
senses.definitionCN: 政策、行动或威胁没能达到预期效果
senses.example: The study exposed the impotence of the city ban.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究揭示了该市禁令形同虚设。
senses.why: A rule with power changes behaviour, while a rule with no power changes nothing, so the word reaches out from people to anything that fails to work.
senses.whyCN: 有力量的规则能改变行为，没有力量的规则什么都改不了，于是这个词从人扩展到一切不起作用的东西。

senses.title: A medical condition in men
senses.definition: a medical condition in which a man is unable to achieve or keep an erection
senses.definitionCN: 男性无法勃起或维持勃起的医学状况
senses.example: The clinic offers treatment for impotence in older men.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所为年长男性提供阳痿治疗。
senses.why: Medical Latin used the word for the power of the male body, so the general lack of power was narrowed to one specific function.
senses.whyCN: 医学拉丁语用这个词指男性身体的能力，于是「普遍的无力量」被收窄成一项具体的功能。

senses.title: A lack of moral or intellectual force
senses.definition: the weakness of character or of thought that stops a person from doing what is right
senses.definitionCN: 性格或思想上的软弱，使人做不到该做的事
senses.example: The novel accuses the government of moral impotence.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说指责政府道德上的软弱。
senses.why: Political writing argues by blaming weakness of will as much as weakness of body, so the word also names a failure of nerve.
senses.whyCN: 政治论战既指责身体虚弱，也指责意志软弱，于是这个词也用来指「没有胆量」。

intro.en: Impotence comes from Latin impotentia, a lack of power or self-control, built from in- (not) on the adjective potens (powerful), which comes from posse, to be able.
intro.cn: impotence 来自拉丁语 impotentia（缺乏力量或自制），由 in-（不）加形容词 potens（有力的）构成，而 potens 又源于 posse（能够）。

items.en: Posse meant to be able; from it came potens, powerful, and the noun potentia, power.
items.cn: posse 意为「能够」；由它派生出 potens（有力的）与名词 potentia（力量）。

items.en: Impotentia meant a lack of power, weakness, or the loss of self-control.
items.cn: impotentia 意为力量不足、虚弱，或失去自制。

items.en: Impotence was first used for bodily weakness and for the lack of self-control.
items.cn: impotence 最早用于指身体虚弱以及缺乏自制。

items.en: The medical sense of a failure of male sexual power appears in this period.
items.cn: 指男性性功能失效的医学义项在这一时期出现。

items.en: Modern usage extends the word to political, social and moral weakness.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词扩展到政治、社会与道德上的软弱。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family of Latin potens and one word that only looks similar; the near-meaning group gathers words for weakness and for being unable to act.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁语 potens 词族，以及一个只是长得像的词；近义组收表示虚弱与无法行动的说法。

entries.definition: the adjective meaning lacking power
entries.definitionCN: 派生形容词，义为「无力的、无能的」；impotence 是它的名词。

entries.definition: powerful, able to have a strong effect, formed without the negative prefix
entries.definitionCN: 同词根的肯定形式，义为「强有力的、有效的」；去掉否定前缀就是它的反面。

entries.definition: existing as a possibility and not yet in action, from the same Latin root of power
entries.definitionCN: 同词根，义为「潜在的、可能的」，指还藏着、尚未发挥的力量。

entries.definition: the quality of mattering a great deal
entries.definitionCN: 义为「重要性」；只是拼写相近，词源不同（来自 importare，与「有力」无关）。

entries.definition: the state of having no power to act
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「无权力、无力」，是平实的直译说法，不带医学色彩。

entries.definition: the state of being unable to look after oneself or to change a situation
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「无助」，强调无人可帮、只能看着。

entries.definition: a lack of physical or moral strength
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「虚弱、弱点」，范围最广，可指身体也可指性格。

entries.definition: the quality of having no use or no result
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，义为「徒劳、无效」，指努力没有结果。

normalIntro.en: Impotence is the Latin word for power with a negative prefix in front of it, so these hooks hang on the real root and on the situations where the word is used.
normalIntro.cn: impotence 就是拉丁语「力量」一词前面加了一个否定前缀，所以下面的记忆钩子都挂在真实词根和实际使用情境上。

normal.en: in- means not and potent- means powerful, so impotence is exactly no power, and potent, potential and potency all sit in the same family.
normal.cn: in- 意为「不」，potent- 意为「有力」，所以 impotence 正是「没有力量」；potent、potential、potency 都在同一个词族里。

normal.en: The adjective impotent is the older English form; the noun impotence follows it and names the state.
normal.cn: 形容词 impotent 在英语里更早出现，名词 impotence 跟随其后，用来指这种状态。

normal.en: In medicine, impotence is the plain term for the inability to keep an erection.
normal.cn: 医学里，impotence 是表示「无法维持勃起」的直白说法。

normal.en: A sense of impotence is what people feel facing a flood, a long illness or a distant government.
normal.cn: a sense of impotence 就是人面对洪水、久病或远方的政府时的那种感受。

normal.en: Compare weakness: weakness is a general lack of strength, while impotence stresses that nothing can be done about it.
normal.cn: 对比 weakness：weakness 是一般的力气不足，impotence 更强调「什么都做不了」。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pressed flat against a heavy door, and the door does not move a finger width.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手掌平平地按在一扇重门上，门连一指宽都不动。

abstract.en: Picture a person pushing a cart with all their strength while the wheels simply spin in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人用尽全力推车，车轮却只在原地空转。

abstract.en: Picture a sign that clearly says the road is closed, and every driver keeps going straight past it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块牌子清楚地写着此路封闭，可每位司机都照样开过去。

examples.en: He was overcome by a feeling of impotence as the fire spread.
examples.cn: 火势蔓延时，他感到一阵无能为力。

examples.en: The report blames the impotence of local officials for the slow rescue.
examples.cn: 报告把救援迟缓归咎于当地官员的无能。

examples.en: Doctors treat impotence as a common condition, not a taboo.
examples.cn: 医生把阳痿视为一种常见状况，而不是禁忌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬怕疼死」——想使劲却使不上劲，只能干着急；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in-（不）+ posse（能够）→ potens（有力的）、potentia（力量）→ impotentia（无力）→ 英语 impotence，核心义「力量被抽走」；同族有 potent、potential、potency。

sensesIntro.en: Impotence is first a lack of power over the world, then a lack inside a body or a will, then the failure of a rule to work, and in medicine one specific failure of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: impotence 先指对世界无能为力，再指身体或意志内部的虚弱，然后是规则失效，医学上则专指身体某一项功能失效。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pushes a heavy door and the door does not shift.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手推着沉重的门，门纹丝不动。

branches.en: The situation branch: a person can see a problem and still cannot act.
branches.cn: 处境分支：人能看见问题，却动不了手。

branches.en: The body branch: the strength inside the person is itself missing.
branches.cn: 身体分支：连人自身的力气也缺了。

branches.en: The policy branch: a rule with no power behind it changes nothing.
branches.cn: 政策分支：背后没有力量的规则什么都改不了。

branches.en: The moral branch: the missing power is the courage to do what is right.
branches.cn: 道德分支：缺的不是力气，而是做正事的胆量。

branches.en: The medical branch: the same denial of power narrows to one function of the male body.
branches.cn: 医学分支：同一个「力量缺失」收窄到男性身体的某一项功能。

intro.en: Impotence is the Latin noun of power with a negative prefix: English keeps impotence and its adjective impotent, and potent, potential and potency form the family with the prefix removed.
intro.cn: impotence 是拉丁语「力量」名词加上否定前缀；英语保留 impotence 与形容词 impotent，而 potent、potential、potency 则是去掉前缀的同一词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin posse means to be able, potens means powerful, potentia means power, and impotentia means a lack of power.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 posse 意为「能够」，potens 意为「有力的」，potentia 意为「力量」，impotentia 意为「无力」。

items.example: Before p the prefix turns into im-, as in impotence.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，前缀 in- 变成 im-，如 impotence。

items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family of power.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个「力量」词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective names something that can act.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词指能够行动之物。

items.example: It is the abstract noun of power.
items.exampleCN: 它是表示「力量」的抽象名词。

items.example: The negative prefix and the root joined to make the word.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀与词根合成了这个词。

items.meaningCN: 形容词词尾：处于……状态的
items.example: The ending turns the stem into the adjective impotent.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把词干变成形容词 impotent。

items.example: The suffix builds the noun impotence from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾由形容词造出名词 impotence。

items.example: The same family gives potency from potent.
items.exampleCN: 同一词族里，potent 加 -cy 得到 potency。

items.example: The family also gives the adjective potential.
items.exampleCN: 这个词族还给出形容词 potential。

definition_zh: 使贫穷；使枯竭；使贫化
definition_en: to make a person, a place or a thing poor, weaker, or poorer in quality
core_image: 一块富饶的田地被一筐筐搬空，只剩下干裂的土
scene: 以前这里是一片果园，如今推土机来过，树被拔走，地皮也卖掉了；整座村子眼看着一点点空下去。The drought impoverished the farmers and emptied their wells.
sceneCN: 这里 impoverish 是「使贫穷」（第 1 个义项：让某人或某地陷入贫困）；句意为旱灾让农民陷入贫困，也抽干了他们的水井。田地被搬空的那幅画面，就是这个词的核心印象。

pos.zh: 使贫穷；使变穷；使枯竭；使（质量）下降

derivatives.zh: impoverish 加 -ment 构成名词，义为「贫困化；贫乏」
过去分词转作形容词，义为「贫困的；贫瘠的」
同源的形容词，义为「贫穷的」，是这个词最日常的说法
pauper 词族的名词，义为「贫困」

senses.title: To make someone or a place poor
senses.definition: to make people, a community or a region poor
senses.definitionCN: 使人、社区或地区变得贫穷
senses.example: The long war impoverished the whole region.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的战争使整个地区陷入贫困。
senses.why: The prefix in- denies the Latin pauper, a poor man, so to impoverish is to push someone into that poor state: the field is emptied dish by dish.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 in- 否定了拉丁语 pauper（穷人），所以 impoverish 就是把某人推进那种穷困状态：田地一筐一筐被搬空。

senses.title: To use up the resources of the land
senses.definition: to reduce the richness of soil, water or land so that it can no longer feed people well
senses.definitionCN: 使土壤、水源或土地的肥力下降，再不能好好养活人
senses.example: Year after year of the same crop impoverishes the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 年年种同一种作物会使土壤贫瘠。
senses.why: The emptied field is not only a picture of money lost but of nutrients taken out, so the word also names land that has lost its substance.
senses.whyCN: 空掉的田不只是钱少了，也是养分被取走了，所以这个词也用来指失去养分的土地。

senses.title: To make a thing poorer in quality
senses.definition: to remove resources of money, ideas or quality from something, leaving it weaker than before
senses.definitionCN: 抽走金钱、思想或质量方面的资源，使某物比以前更薄弱
senses.example: Budget cuts impoverish the work of schools.
senses.exampleCN: 预算削减使学校的工作打了折扣。
senses.why: Anything that has resources can be stripped of them, so schools, health services and research can be impoverished just like families.
senses.whyCN: 凡是有资源的东西都能被抽空，所以学校、医疗与研究也会像家庭一样被搬空。

senses.title: To make experience or language poorer
senses.definition: to make the life, mind or vocabulary of a person narrower by taking away what enriches it
senses.definitionCN: 拿走丰富人生的东西，使人的生活、心智或词汇变得狭小
senses.example: A childhood without books impoverishes the imagination.
senses.exampleCN: 没有书的童年会让想象力变得贫乏。
senses.why: The same emptying applies to the inside of a person: a mind or a language that loses words and ideas is poorer in the same way a village is.
senses.whyCN: 这种「搬空」也发生在人心里：失去词语与想法的头脑或语言，就像村子一样变得更穷。

intro.en: Impoverish comes from Old French empovrir, to make poor, which in turn rests on Latin pauper, a poor man; an -ish ending was attached to the French stem in English.
intro.cn: impoverish 来自古法语 empovrir（使变穷），后者源于拉丁语 pauper（穷人）；英语在法语词干后接上了 -ish。

items.en: Pauper meant poor or, as a noun, a poor man; its origin is thought to lie in a word for small or scanty produce.
items.cn: pauper 意为「贫穷的」，作名词指「穷人」；一般认为它源于一个表示「产量少」的词。

items.en: The verb empovrir meant to make poor, and the adjective povre meant poor.
items.cn: 古法语动词 empovrir 意为「使变穷」，形容词 povre 意为「贫穷的」。

items.en: Impoverish appears in English writing, with the French stem and an English verb ending.
items.cn: impoverish 出现在英语文献中，由法语词干加英语动词词尾构成。

items.en: The meaning widens from money to land, wells and other resources that are worn out or used up.
items.cn: 词义从金钱扩展到土地、水井等资源被耗尽、变差的情形。

items.en: Modern usage also speaks of an impoverished vocabulary, memory or imagination.
items.cn: 现代用法也会说 vocabulary、memory 或 imagination 被 impoverish，指思想与表达变得贫乏。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pauper family and one word built with the same -ish ending; the near-meaning group gathers words for reducing wealth, strength or quality.
note.cn: 形近组收 pauper 词族与一个同样带 -ish 的词；近义组收表示减少财富、力量或质量的说法。

entries.definition: made poor, as an adjective
entries.definitionCN: 派生形容词，义为「贫困的、贫瘠的」，如 impoverished families。

entries.definition: the noun naming the process of being made poor
entries.definitionCN: 派生名词，义为「贫困化、贫乏」，指变穷的过程。

entries.definition: the state of being poor, from the same Latin pauper
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「贫困」，同出于拉丁语 pauper。

entries.definition: to bring out a book or a text for the public; only the ending and spelling are close, since the root is different
entries.definitionCN: 义为「出版、发表」；只是词尾与拼写相近，词源不同（来自 publicare）。

entries.definition: poor, or having lost resources
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「贫困的」，是这个词最常用的形容词形式，常作定语。

entries.definition: to reduce the amount of something until very little is left
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「耗尽、使枯竭」，强调数量被大量减少。

entries.definition: to take the strength or the resources out of something gradually
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「抽干、耗掉」，多用作比喻，如 drain resources。

entries.definition: to make someone or something less strong
entries.definitionCN: 近义，义为「削弱」，侧重力量减弱，不一定涉及钱财。

normalIntro.en: Impoverish belongs to the small family of Latin pauper, so these hooks work from the real root and from the things the word is said of.
normalIntro.cn: impoverish 属于拉丁语 pauper 这个小词族，所以下面的记忆钩子都从真实词根和它常被用来谈论的对象入手。

normal.en: The stem pover- and the adjective poor both go back to Latin pauper, so impoverish and poor are cousins.
normal.cn: 词干 pover- 与形容词 poor 都回溯到拉丁语 pauper，两者同宗。

normal.en: The -ish ending makes a verb out of the French stem, as in finish or establish.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ish 让法语词干变成动词，类似 finish、establish 的构词方式。

normal.en: Soil, wells and forests can be impoverished, so the word is not only about money.
normal.cn: 土壤、水井、森林都可以被 impoverish，所以这个词不只谈钱。

normal.en: Impoverished is the usual adjective, as in an impoverished region or an impoverished diet.
normal.cn: impoverished 是最常用的形容词形式，如 an impoverished region「贫困地区」、an impoverished diet「营养贫乏的饮食」。

normal.en: Compare deplete: deplete counts what is taken away, while impoverish says what the result is.
normal.cn: 对比 deplete：deplete 侧重「被拿走了多少」，impoverish 侧重「结果变穷了」。

abstract.en: Picture a rich field with baskets carried away one by one until only dry soil is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一块肥沃的田，一筐一筐被搬走，最后只剩干裂的土。

abstract.en: Picture a well whose water level drops a little lower each year, and the bucket comes up half empty.
abstract.cn: 想象一口井，水位每年低一点，桶提上来时只剩半桶。

abstract.en: Picture a warm house slowly stripped of furniture, leaving empty rooms and cold air.
abstract.cn: 想象一座温暖的房子被一件件搬空了家具，只剩空房间和冷风。

examples.en: Heavy taxes impoverished the small farmers.
examples.cn: 沉重的赋税使小农陷入贫困。

examples.en: Planting the same crop every year impoverishes the soil.
examples.cn: 年年种植同一种作物会使土壤贫瘠。

examples.en: Years of neglect had impoverished the music programme of the school.
examples.cn: 多年的忽视使学校的音乐课程变得贫乏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬破窝里什」——家里硬是被破光了，什物都没剩下，就是变穷；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 pauper（贫穷的；穷人）→ 古法语 empovrir（使变穷）→ 英语 impoverish，核心义「把富足的东西一件件抽走」；同族有 poor、poverty、impoverished。

sensesIntro.en: Impoverish starts with money, then spreads to land, to any resource and finally to the mind, as one after another kind of richness is taken away.
sensesIntro.cn: impoverish 先谈钱，再谈土地，再谈任何资源，最后谈心智：一种又一种富足被拿走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rich field is carried off basket by basket until only dry soil remains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块肥沃的田被一筐筐搬空，只剩干裂的土。

branches.en: The money branch: war and taxes push people and places into poverty.
branches.cn: 金钱分支：战争与赋税把人、把地方推进贫困。

branches.en: The land branch: the same crop and the same field drain its strength.
branches.cn: 土地分支：同一种作物、同一块田，把地力耗干。

branches.en: The resource branch: schools and services lose money and quality together.
branches.cn: 资源分支：学校与服务一起失去经费与质量。

branches.en: The mind branch: a life without books loses its words and pictures.
branches.cn: 心智分支：没有书的生活失去词语与画面。

branches.en: The emptying branch: whether soil or memory, richness is taken out by the same motion.
branches.cn: 搬空分支：无论是土壤还是记忆，富足都以同样的动作被拿走。

intro.en: Impoverish is a Latin root of poverty carried through Old French, with an English verb ending; the family includes poor, poverty, impoverishment and impoverished.
intro.cn: impoverish 是以「贫穷」这一拉丁词根经古法语传入、加上英语动词词尾得到的；同族有 poor、poverty、impoverishment 与 impoverished。

latinIntro.en: Latin pauper means poor; its deeper origin is uncertain, though it is generally thought to come from a word for scanty produce.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pauper 意为「贫穷的」；更深一层的来源不确定，一般认为来自表示「产量稀少」的词。

items.example: Before p the prefix becomes im-, as in impoverish.
items.exampleCN: 在 p 之前，前缀 in- 变成 im-，如 impoverish。

items.example: The root supplies the whole idea of poverty.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供了「贫穷」的全部含义。

items.example: The stem reaches English through the French form of pauper.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干经 pauper 的法语形式进入英语。

items.example: The ending turns the French stem into a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把法语词干变成动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示已受到的动作或状态
items.example: It forms impoverished and its adjective use.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 impoverished 及其形容词用法。

items.example: It forms impoverishing.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 impoverishing。

items.example: The suffix forms impoverishment.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾构成 impoverishment。

items.example: The old short form of pauper survives as poor.
items.exampleCN: pauper 的古旧短形式留成了 poor。

items.example: The family also gives poverty from the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根还给出名词 poverty。

definition_zh: 不精确的；不准确的；含糊的；不严谨的
definition_en: not exact, accurate, or clearly defined, so that details are vague or approximate
core_image: 一杆刻度被磨掉的尺子，量出来的长度总是差一点
scene: 实验报告里的测量结果只写了一个大概的数值，导师看后圈出几处指出描述过于含糊。The supervisor circled several points and said the description of the procedure was too imprecise to be repeated.
sceneCN: 这里 imprecise 是「不精确、含糊」（第 2 个义项：表述或描述缺乏细节）；句意：导师圈出几处，说操作过程的描述太含糊，无法照着重做。

pos.zh: 不精确的；不准确的；含糊的

collocations.zh: 不精确的语言；含混的措辞
对……说得不准确；在……上含糊

derivatives.zh: 不准确；含糊（由 imprecise 加名词后缀 -ion 构成）
不精确地；含糊地（由 imprecise 加副词后缀 -ly 构成）
精确的（去掉否定前缀 im- 的基础形容词）
精确；精密（precise 加名词后缀 -ion）

senses.title: Not exact as a measurement
senses.definition: not exact in measure, amount, or value, so the figure is only approximate
senses.definitionCN: 在计量、数量或数值上不精确，给出的数字只是近似的
senses.example: The instrument gave an imprecise reading and the team repeated the test.
senses.exampleCN: 仪器给出的读数不精确，于是团队重新做了测试。
senses.why: The Latin verb praecidere means to cut off, and the prefix im- negates it, so what is imprecise has not been trimmed to an exact edge.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语动词 praecidere 本义「切去」，前缀 im- 表示否定；所以不精确就是没被削到那个恰好齐整的边。

senses.title: Vague in language
senses.definition: using words that are vague and do not give clear detail
senses.definitionCN: 用词含糊，没有给出清楚的细节
senses.example: He was imprecise about when the report would be ready.
senses.exampleCN: 他对报告什么时候能完成说得含糊不清。
senses.why: A statement is also an edge to be cut: an imprecise sentence leaves the boundary of meaning loose.
senses.whyCN: 一句话同样是一条要被削齐的边：不精确的句子，意思的边界是松的。

senses.title: Loose in definition
senses.definition: not defined in a strict or consistent way, especially in official or scholarly use
senses.definitionCN: 定义得不严格或不一致，尤见于官方或学术用法
senses.example: The committee rejected the regulation because its wording was imprecise.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会否决了这项规定，因为它的措辞不够严谨。
senses.why: Laws and definitions need a clean cut between what is included and excluded; imprecise wording lets the two sides blur.
senses.whyCN: 法规与定义需要在「包括」与「不包括」之间划出干净的一刀；措辞不精确，两边就会糊在一起。

senses.title: Roughly done
senses.definition: done without care or fine detail
senses.definitionCN: 做得不细致、缺乏精细处理
senses.example: The early maps of the coast were imprecise and often wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 早期的海岸地图很粗糙，而且常常出错。
senses.why: The same lack of a clean edge shows up in work that has been roughed out rather than finished.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「边没削齐」也体现在活干得毛糙、没有收尾上，于是引申为粗糙。

senses.title: Not accurately recalled
senses.definition: remembered only roughly, with details missing or altered
senses.definitionCN: 只记得个大概，细节缺失或有偏差
senses.example: My memory of that evening is imprecise, but I remember the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 那晚的记忆已不清晰，但我记得下着雨。
senses.why: A memory is an impression with an edge, and imprecise recall is an impression that never got cut sharply.
senses.whyCN: 记忆也是一块有边的印子；回忆不精确，就是那块印子始终没被削清楚。

senses.title: Sloppy or careless
senses.definition: careless in method or habit, so results cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 方法或习惯上马虎，结果不可靠
senses.example: His imprecise habits made it hard to check his work.
senses.exampleCN: 他做事不严谨的习惯让人很难核对他的工作。
senses.why: When precision is a habit of cutting cleanly, its absence becomes a character trait we can name.
senses.whyCN: 当精确成了一种「下刀干净」的习惯，它的缺席就成了一种可以点名的性格特征。

senses.title: Not strict about details
senses.definition: showing a relaxed standard that allows small differences to pass
senses.definitionCN: 标准宽松，允许细小差异存在
senses.example: The coach is imprecise about shoe type and only asks for stable footing.
senses.exampleCN: 教练对鞋的款式并不苛求，只要求站得稳。
senses.why: Someone who never insists on the exact edge is by nature relaxed about detail.
senses.whyCN: 从不计较那条精确的边的人，自然对细节比较宽松。

intro.en: Imprecise is the negative of precise, which comes to English through Middle French précis from Latin praecisus, the past participle of praecidere, to cut off.
intro.cn: imprecise 是 precise 的否定形式；precise 经中古法语 précis 来自拉丁语 praecisus，即 praecidere（切去）的过去分词。

items.en: Praecidere, from prae before and caedere to cut, means to cut off in front.
items.cn: praecidere 由 prae（在前）与 caedere（切）构成，意为在前面切去。

items.en: The participle praecisus means cut short or trimmed, and gives the sense of a clearly bounded thing.
items.cn: 分词 praecisus 意为被切短、削齐，由此引申出边界清楚的含义。

items.en: Old French and Middle French precis develop the meaning exact, trimmed to the point.
items.cn: 古法语与中古法语 précis 发展出「精确、恰好切到点」的意思。

items.en: Precise enters English meaning exact and clearly defined.
items.cn: precise 进入英语，表示精确、定义清楚。

items.en: The prefix in- with its im- form is attached to precise to form imprecise, meaning not exact.
items.cn: 否定前缀 in- 在 p 前变作 im- 加在 precise 上，构成 imprecise，表示不精确。

items.en: Imprecise spreads from measurement to language, law, and manners.
items.cn: imprecise 从测量领域扩展到语言、法律与行为举止。

note.en: Imprecise sits in a family built on precise, and near a cluster of words for inexactness and vagueness.
note.cn: imprecise 属于以 precise 为核心的词族，同时与一批表示「不准确、含糊」的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of not being exact
entries.definitionCN: 不精确；含糊（imprecise 加名词后缀的同族词）

entries.definition: in a way that is not exact
entries.definitionCN: 不精确地；含糊地

entries.definition: not showing good judgement
entries.definitionCN: 不谨慎的（只与目标词共享否定前缀 im-，词源不同）

entries.definition: not likely to happen
entries.definitionCN: 不大可能的（只与目标词共享否定前缀 im-，词源不同）

entries.definition: not clear or definite in meaning
entries.definitionCN: 含糊的；不明确的

entries.definition: not exact or detailed
entries.definitionCN: 粗略的；大致的

entries.definition: not strict or exact
entries.definitionCN: 宽松的；不严谨的

entries.definition: not correct or exact
entries.definitionCN: 不准确的

normalIntro.en: Im- negates precise, and precise pictures something cut cleanly to an exact measure.
normalIntro.cn: im- 表示否定，而 precise 的画面是「被切得刚刚好、分毫不差」。

normal.en: Take precise, whose Latin root is a verb meaning to cut off, and put im- in front of it.
normal.cn: 把 precise 拿来，它的拉丁词根是「切去」，前面再加表否定的 im-。

normal.en: The pair precise and imprecise differ only by two letters at the front.
normal.cn: precise 与 imprecise 只差开头两个字母，成对记住更牢。

normal.en: An imprecise measurement gives a figure with a wide margin.
normal.cn: imprecise measurement 指给出宽误差范围的读数。

normal.en: Imprecise language leaves the reader guessing what the writer meant.
normal.cn: imprecise language 让读者只能猜作者的意思。

normal.en: Compare inaccurate, which stresses being wrong, while imprecise stresses lacking sharp detail.
normal.cn: 对比 inaccurate：前者强调「错」，imprecise 强调「不锋利、缺细节」。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose markings have worn away, so every reading is a little off.
abstract.cn: 想象一把刻度被磨掉的尺子，每次量出来的都差一点。

abstract.en: Imagine a scalpel that has lost its edge, leaving the cut ragged instead of clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钝了的刀，切口毛糙而不是干净利落。

abstract.en: Think of a law that says punishment for bad behaviour, without saying what bad means.
abstract.cn: 想象一条法规只说「对不良行为予以处罚」，却没说何为不良。

examples.en: The survey results were too imprecise to support a firm conclusion.
examples.cn: 调查结果不够精确，无法支撑明确结论。

examples.en: Try to avoid imprecise words such as many or soon in the contract.
examples.cn: 合同里要尽量避免 many 或 soon 这类不精确的词。

examples.en: Tourists often have only an imprecise idea of the city boundary.
examples.cn: 游客对城市边界的了解往往只是大概。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「im + 坏刀切菜」——刀不够锋利，切出来的边都是毛的，就是不精确；这只是谐音拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 praecidere（prae 在前 + caedere 切去）→ 过去分词 praecisus（被削齐的）→ 中古法语 précis → 英语 precise；加否定前缀 in- 的变体 im- 构成 imprecise，核心义「没被削到恰好的那条边」。

sensesIntro.en: Imprecise begins with readings that miss the exact value, moves to sentences that leave meaning loose, and ends with a person who is relaxed about detail.
sensesIntro.cn: imprecise 先指读数没有命中精确值，再指句子让意思松动，最后指一个人对细节比较宽松。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler whose markings have worn away, so every reading is a little off.
core.cn: 核心意象：刻度被磨掉的尺子，每次量出来都差一点。

branches.en: A reading that never lands on the exact figure is the measuring sense.
branches.cn: 始终落不到精确数值上的读数，是计量义项。

branches.en: Words and definitions that do not mark their own limits are the language sense.
branches.cn: 词句与定义划不清自身边界，是语言义项。

branches.en: Rough work and fuzzy memory both lack the same clean edge.
branches.cn: 粗糙的成品与模糊的记忆，都缺了那条干净的边。

branches.en: A person who never insists on the exact edge reads as sloppy or relaxed.
branches.cn: 从不在精确边上较真的人，就显出马虎或宽松。

branches.en: Measurement, prose, and law all suffer when boundaries blur.
branches.cn: 边界一旦模糊，测量、文句与法规都会受损。

intro.en: Imprecise is built from the negating prefix im-, the root for cutting, and the adjective ending -e carried over from precise.
intro.cn: imprecise 由表否定的前缀 im-、表示「切」的词根构成，并沿用了 precise 词尾的形容词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin praecidere, from prae and caedere, means to cut off; its participle praecisus gives precise.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 praecidere 由 prae 与 caedere 构成，意为切去；其分词 praecisus 给出 precise。

items.example: The prefix im- turns precise into imprecise.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 把 precise 变成 imprecise。

items.example: The prefix in- becomes im- before p, b, and m.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 在 p、b、m 之前变作 im-。

items.example: The prefix prae- gives the front position in praecidere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 prae- 在 praecidere 中表示「在前」。

items.example: Caedere supplies the image of cutting.
items.exampleCN: caedere 提供「切」的画面。

items.example: Praecidere is the source of the exact meaning.
items.exampleCN: praecidere 是「精确」义的来源。

items.example: The participle ending -isus yields praecisus.
items.exampleCN: 分词词尾 -isus 构成 praecisus。

items.example: The base adjective precise arrived through French.
items.exampleCN: 基础形容词 precise 经法语传入英语。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ion forms imprecision.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 imprecision。

items.example: Imprecision names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: imprecision 指这种性质本身。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms imprecisely.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 imprecisely。

definition_zh: 不得体；失礼；不当行为；用词不当
definition_en: behaviour or language that is not proper, polite, or acceptable in a given situation
core_image: 本该穿正装的场合，有人穿了拖鞋走进来
scene: 一场正式的听证会结束后，社交账号出现了一条措辞失礼的评论，主办方随即发表声明致歉。After the hearing, a comment with clear impropriety appeared online, and the organisers issued a statement of apology.
sceneCN: 这里 impropriety 是「不得体、失礼」（第 1 个义项：行为或言论不合场合）；句意：听证会之后，网上出现了一条明显失礼的评论，主办方随即发表声明致歉。

derivatives.zh: 不恰当的；不得体的（去掉名词后缀 -iety 得到的形容词）
不恰当地（improper 加副词后缀 -ly）
得体；礼节（去掉否定前缀 im- 的正面名词）
合适的；得体的（最基础的形式）

senses.title: Bad conduct in a situation
senses.definition: behaviour that is not suitable or acceptable in a particular situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定场合中不合适、不被接受的行为
senses.example: A guest making a speech at a funeral would be guilty of impropriety.
senses.exampleCN: 在葬礼上长篇致辞的宾客就是行为不得体。
senses.why: Proper comes from Latin proprius, one own, and impropriety is conduct that is not proper for the occasion.
senses.whyCN: proper 源自拉丁语 proprius（属于某人自己的），所以 impropriety 是「不属于这个场合该有」的举止。

senses.title: Official misconduct
senses.definition: wrongdoing or misconduct by a person in a position of public trust
senses.definitionCN: 受公众信任之人的不当行为或失职
senses.example: The inspector resigned after allegations of financial impropriety.
senses.exampleCN: 监察员在财务不当行为的指控出现后辞职。
senses.why: When the standard is set by public office, a lapse from propriety becomes a matter of misconduct.
senses.whyCN: 当标准由公职身份来定，偏离「得体」就升级为失职与不当。

senses.title: Unacceptable in law
senses.definition: an act that is ruled improper in a legal or formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 在法律或正式场合被判定为不当的行为
senses.example: The judge found no impropriety in the way the jury was chosen.
senses.exampleCN: 法官认定陪审团的遴选方式没有问题。
senses.why: Courts judge each act against a formal standard, so impropriety becomes the legal name for a step out of line.
senses.whyCN: 法庭用正式标准逐一衡量每个举动，于是 impropriety 成了「越线一步」的法律称呼。

senses.title: Unacceptable language
senses.definition: a word or phrase that is unsuitable or does not fit the context
senses.definitionCN: 不适合语境或使用不当的词句
senses.example: The editor cut several improprieties from the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑删掉了信里几处用词不当的地方。
senses.why: The same standard applies to words: language that does not belong to the occasion is an impropriety.
senses.whyCN: 同一把尺子也量语言：不属于这个场合的措辞，就是一次用词不当。

senses.title: Social awkwardness
senses.definition: a minor social slip that causes embarrassment
senses.definitionCN: 造成尴尬的小小社交失误
senses.example: His joke about the divorce was a social impropriety that no one forgot.
senses.exampleCN: 他那句关于离婚的玩笑是一个没人忘得掉的社交失态。
senses.why: Not every lapse is a scandal; the word also names small social misfits that leave the room quiet.
senses.whyCN: 并非每次失当都是丑闻；这个词也指那种让整个房间安静下来的小小失态。

senses.title: Plural wrongdoings
senses.definition: several separate acts that are improper or illegal
senses.definitionCN: 若干起各自不当或违法的行为
senses.example: The audit listed a series of improprieties in the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计在账目中列出了一系列不当行为。
senses.why: When one impropriety repeats, the plural counts the separate acts.
senses.whyCN: 当一次失当反复出现，复数形式就是把这些行为一件件数出来。

senses.title: Quiet suspicion
senses.definition: a suggestion or appearance of something improper rather than a proven act
senses.definitionCN: 让人觉得不妥的迹象或嫌疑，而非已证实的行为
senses.example: The adviser avoided any appearance of impropriety by declaring her shares.
senses.exampleCN: 顾问公开申报自己的股份，以免有任何有失妥当之嫌。
senses.why: Even the look of a misfit is enough to be called an impropriety, so the word often appears with appearance.
senses.whyCN: 有时候只是「看着不对劲」就足以称为 impropriety，因此它常与 appearance 一起出现。

senses.title: Careless mistake
senses.definition: a slip or error made without proper care
senses.definitionCN: 因不够谨慎而犯下的疏漏或差错
senses.example: Loose files on the desk were the only impropriety the auditors found.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上散乱的文件是审计员发现的唯一疏漏。
senses.why: If propriety is a habit of carefulness, a careless slip is impropriety in miniature.
senses.whyCN: 如果得体是一种用心的习惯，那么粗心的疏漏就是小号的不得体。

intro.en: Impropriety comes from Latin improprius, not one own, formed from in- not and proprius belonging to oneself, through Old French impropriete or directly.
intro.cn: impropriety 来自拉丁语 improprius（不专属的），由 in-（不）与 proprius（属于自己的）构成，可能经古法语 impropriete 传入英语。

items.en: Proprius means one own or belonging to a particular person.
items.cn: proprius 意为「某人自己的、专属于某人的」。

items.en: The adjective improprius means not belonging to oneself, hence unsuitable.
items.cn: 形容词 improprius 表示「不专属的」，引申为「不合适的」。

items.en: The noun improprietas names the quality of being unfit.
items.cn: 名词 improprietas 表示「不合适」的性质。

items.en: Old French impropriete carries the word, and propriete gives English propriety.
items.cn: 古法语 impropriete 传下这个词，而 propriete 则给出英语 propriety。

items.en: Impropriety appears in English meaning a fault against fitness and good manners.
items.cn: impropriety 进入英语，表示违背适宜与礼仪的过失。

items.en: Modern use adds formal and legal misconduct and plural wrongdoings.
items.cn: 现代用法增加了正式的失职指控与复数的不当行为。

note.en: Impropriety is the noun of not-fitting; it looks close to the proprius family and means close to rudeness and misconduct.
note.cn: impropriety 是「不合宜」的名词；形式上接近 proprius 词族，意义上接近无礼与失职。

entries.definition: to put church property under lay control, an obsolete formal use
entries.definitionCN: 把教会财产转归俗人控制（罕见的正式旧义，同源于 proprius）

entries.definition: not suitable or correct
entries.definitionCN: 不合适的；不得体的

entries.definition: relating to ownership
entries.definitionCN: 专有的；所有权的

entries.definition: something owned
entries.definitionCN: 财产（同源于 proprius「自己的」）

entries.definition: behaviour that offends accepted standards of decency
entries.definitionCN: 无礼；下流

entries.definition: unacceptable behaviour, especially by an official
entries.definitionCN: 不当行为；失职

entries.definition: lack of polite behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 无礼；粗鲁

entries.definition: a careless and serious mistake
entries.definitionCN: 愚蠢的错误

normalIntro.en: Impropriety is im- plus propriety; propriety is what fits, so impropriety is what does not fit.
normalIntro.cn: impropriety 是 im- 加 propriety；propriety 是「合宜」，加了 im- 就是「不合宜」。

normal.en: The prefix im- negates the noun propriety, and the whole word is a single noun with plural improprieties.
normal.cn: 前缀 im- 否定名词 propriety，整体是不可数名词，复数形式为 improprieties。

normal.en: The root proprius means one own, and the propriety family includes proper, properly, and proprietary.
normal.cn: 词根 proprius 意为「自己的」，同族词包括 proper、properly 与 proprietary。

normal.en: Financial impropriety is the regular pairing in news reports about officials.
normal.cn: financial impropriety 是新闻里谈官员时最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The phrase appearance of impropriety means even the suspicion looks bad.
normal.cn: appearance of impropriety 指连「看起来可疑」都要避免。

normal.en: Compare misbehaviour, which is ordinary and broad, with impropriety, which is formal and stresses the wrong setting.
normal.cn: 对比 misbehaviour：后者普通宽泛，impropriety 更正式，强调「错的场合」。

abstract.en: Picture someone in slippers walking into a room where everyone else wears a suit.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人穿着拖鞋走进满屋子正装的房间。

abstract.en: Imagine an official signature that belongs to a document someone else should have signed.
abstract.cn: 想象一个官员的签名出现在本该由别人签的文件上。

abstract.en: Think of a joke in an obituary: the words are not rude, only out of place.
abstract.cn: 想象在讣告里插一句笑话：话不难听，只是放错了地方。

examples.en: The minister denied any impropriety in the award of the contract.
examples.cn: 部长否认在合同授予上有任何不当行为。

examples.en: Even the appearance of impropriety can end a career.
examples.cn: 哪怕只是有失妥当之嫌，也可能断送一个人的职业生涯。

examples.en: The firm has strict rules against financial improprieties.
examples.cn: 这家公司有严格规定禁止财务上的不当行为。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「硬扑不来」——该守的规矩硬是扑不进去，做出来就是不得体；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 proprius（属于自己的、专属的）→ 加否定前缀 in- 构成 improprius（不专属的、不合适的）→ improprietas → 古法语 impropriete → 英语 impropriety，核心义「不合宜」，即「不属于这个场合的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Impropriety starts as acts that do not suit the occasion, extends to official and legal misconduct, and covers unsuitable words, small social slips, and mere suspicion.
sensesIntro.cn: impropriety 先指不适合场合的举止，再扩展到公职与法律上的失职，也覆盖用词不当、小小的社交失态，乃至仅仅的嫌疑。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone in slippers walking into a room where everyone else wears a suit.
core.cn: 核心意象：有人穿着拖鞋走进满屋子正装的房间。

branches.en: Behaviour that does not suit the occasion is the basic social sense.
branches.cn: 不符合场合的举止，是最基本的社会义项。

branches.en: Official and legal settings turn the same misfit into misconduct.
branches.cn: 公职与法律场合把同样的不合宜升级为失职。

branches.en: Language judged by the same standard becomes an impropriety of wording.
branches.cn: 用同一把尺子衡量语言，就得到用词不当。

branches.en: Small social slips and careless errors are impropriety in miniature.
branches.cn: 小小的社交失态与疏漏，都是缩小版的不得体。

branches.en: The plural counts separate acts, while suspicion names the mere look of wrong.
branches.cn: 复数把行为一件件数出，而嫌疑义只指「看起来不对劲」。

intro.en: Impropriety is the negated form of propriety, and the family runs from proper through propriety to proprietary.
intro.cn: impropriety 是 propriety 的否定形式，整个词族从 proper 经 propriety 延伸到 proprietary。

latinIntro.en: Latin proprius means belonging to oneself, and improprius negates it; the noun improprietas gives the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 proprius 意为「属于自己的」，improprius 加以否定；名词 improprietas 给出英语词。

items.example: The prefix im- turns propriety into impropriety.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 im- 把 propriety 变成 impropriety。

items.meaning: one own, belonging to a person
items.example: Proprius is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: proprius 是整个词族的词根。

items.example: Improprius adds the negative to proprius.
items.exampleCN: improprius 在 proprius 前加了否定。

items.meaningCN: 表示性质或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -etas forms improprietas.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -etas 构成 improprietas。

items.meaningCN: 经法语演变的性质词尾
items.example: The suffix -iety forms impropriety from its Latin shape.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -iety 由拉丁形式演变出 impropriety。

items.example: The adjective proper shows the plain root sense.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 proper 体现词根本义。

items.example: Propriety is the positive counterpart of the word.
items.exampleCN: propriety 是它的肯定对应词。

items.example: The adjective improper replaces the noun ending.
items.exampleCN: 形容词 improper 取代了名词词尾。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms improperly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 improperly。

items.example: Proprietary keeps the ownership sense of proprius.
items.exampleCN: proprietary 保留了 proprius 的所有权含义。
